sentences.zh: 鄒緝，字仲熙，吉水人。

translations.literal: Zou Ji, styled Zhongxi, was a native of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Ji, whose style was Zhongxi, came from Jishui.

sentences.zh: 洪武中舉明經，授星子教諭。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu reign he passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed instructor at Xingzi.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hongwu era he passed the Mingjing examination and was made instructor at Xingzi.

sentences.zh: 建文時入為國子助教。

translations.literal: During the Jianwen reign he entered service as an assistant instructor at the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Jianwen he entered the capital as an assistant instructor at the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，擢翰林侍講。

translations.literal: When the Chengzu Emperor took the throne, he was promoted to Hanlin Academician Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor came to the throne, he was promoted to Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 立東宮，兼左中允，屢署國子監事。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Palace was established, he also served as Left Household Administer and repeatedly acted in charge of Directorate of Education affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the crown prince was installed, he also served as Left Household Administer and was repeatedly put in charge of Directorate of Education affairs.

sentences.zh: 永樂十九年，三殿災，詔求直言，緝上疏曰：

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Yongle, the three main halls burned; an edict sought forthright counsel, and Ji submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Yongle, fire destroyed the three main palace halls; the emperor issued an edict calling for frank counsel, and Zou Ji submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 陛下肇建北京，焦勞聖慮，幾二十年。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, at the founding of Beijing, has worn yourself with sage concern for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has labored to build Beijing, bearing the cares of state for nearly twenty years.

sentences.zh: 工大費繁，調度甚廣，冗官蠶食，耗費國儲。

translations.literal: The works are vast, expenses heavy, requisitions very wide; superfluous officials gnaw away and drain the national stores.
translations.idiomatic: The projects are enormous and costly, requisitions stretch far and wide, redundant officials nibble away at resources, and the state granaries are being drained.

sentences.zh: 工作之夫，動以百萬，終歲供役，不得躬親田畝以事力作。

translations.literal: Laborers on the works commonly number in the hundreds of thousands; they serve corvée the whole year and cannot themselves tend their fields for productive toil.
translations.idiomatic: Workers on these projects routinely number in the millions; conscripted for service year-round, they cannot tend their own fields or earn their living by honest labor.

sentences.zh: 猶且征求無藝，至伐桑棗以供薪，剝桑皮以為楮。

translations.literal: Moreover levies are boundless, even to felling mulberry and jujube for firewood and stripping mulberry bark for paper.
translations.idiomatic: On top of this, exactions know no limit—mulberry and jujube trees are cut for fuel, and mulberry bark is stripped to make paper.

sentences.zh: 加之官吏橫征，日甚一日。

translations.literal: Added to this, officials levy arbitrarily, day by day more severe.
translations.idiomatic: Officials add arbitrary levies that grow worse by the day.

sentences.zh: 如前歲買辦顏料，本非土產，動科千百。

translations.literal: As in the year before last, when pigments were purchased though not local products, households were levied by the thousands and hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Take the purchase of pigments two years ago: they were not local products, yet households were assessed by the thousands.

sentences.zh: 民相率斂鈔，購之他所。

translations.literal: The people together pooled paper money to buy them elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: People pooled their paper money to buy them from other regions.

sentences.zh: 大青一斤，價至萬六千貫。

translations.literal: One jin of azurite reached a price of sixteen thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: A single jin of azurite cost as much as sixteen thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 及進納，又多留難，往復展轉，當須二萬貫鈔，而不足供一柱之用。

translations.literal: When presented for delivery, officials again made difficulties; going back and forth, twenty thousand strings of cash were needed yet still insufficient for one pillar's use.
translations.idiomatic: When it came time to deliver the goods, officials obstructed and delayed again and again; after all the back-and-forth, twenty thousand strings of cash might still not suffice to supply a single pillar.

sentences.zh: 其後既遣官采之產所，而買辦猶未止。

translations.literal: Afterward, although officials were sent to gather it at its place of production, purchase levies still did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Even after officials were sent to collect pigments at their source, purchase requisitions still did not stop.

sentences.zh: 蓋緣工匠多派牟利，而不顧民艱至此。

translations.literal: This was because craftsmen, widely assigned, sought profit and did not regard the people's hardship until it reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: The reason is that craftsmen assigned to the work profited from the trade and paid no heed to the people's hardship until matters reached this pass.

sentences.zh: 夫京師天下根本。

translations.literal: The capital is the root of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The capital is the foundation of the realm.

sentences.zh: 人民安則京師安，京師安則國本固而天下安。

translations.literal: If the people are secure, the capital is secure; if the capital is secure, the state's foundation is firm and all under Heaven is secure.
translations.idiomatic: When the people are at peace, the capital is at peace; when the capital is at peace, the foundation of the state is secure and the realm is at peace.

sentences.zh: 自營建以來，工匠小人假托威勢，驅迫移徙，號令方施，廬舍已壞。

translations.literal: Since construction began, petty craftsmen have borrowed authority, driven people to move, and before the order was even issued their dwellings were already destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Since construction began, petty craftsmen have abused their power, forcing people to relocate—the order has scarcely been issued before their homes are torn down.

sentences.zh: 孤兒寡婦哭泣叫號，倉皇暴露，莫知所適。

translations.literal: Orphans and widows wept and cried out, cast out in haste with nowhere to go.
translations.idiomatic: Orphans and widows wept and wailed, cast out in panic with nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 遷移甫定，又復驅令他徒，至有三四徙不得息者。

translations.literal: Hardly had relocation settled when they were driven to move again; some were relocated three or four times without rest.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had one move been settled when they were driven to move again; some were uprooted three or four times without respite.

sentences.zh: 及其既去，而所空之地，經月逾時，工猶未及。

translations.literal: When they had gone, the land they vacated, for months on end, still had no work begun upon it.
translations.idiomatic: After they had been driven away, the land they vacated stood empty for months before work even began.

sentences.zh: 此陛下所不知，而人民疾怨者也。

translations.literal: This Your Majesty does not know, yet the people resent it bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: This is what Your Majesty does not know, yet what fills the people with bitter resentment.

sentences.zh: 貪官汙吏，遍布內外，剝削及於骨髓。

translations.literal: Greedy and corrupt officials are spread inside and outside, their exactions reaching to the marrow.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy, corrupt officials are everywhere, inside and out, squeezing the people to the bone.

sentences.zh: 朝廷每遣一人，即是其人養活之計。

translations.literal: Whenever the court sends out one man, that becomes his means of livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Every envoy the court sends out treats the mission as his personal livelihood.

sentences.zh: 虐取苛求，初無限量。

translations.literal: Cruel seizure and harsh demand know no limit at the outset.
translations.idiomatic: Their extortion and harsh demands know no bounds.

sentences.zh: 有司承奉，惟恐不及。

translations.literal: Local officials in receiving them fear only that they will fall short.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials vie to please them, fearful only of falling short.

sentences.zh: 間有廉強自守、不事幹媚者，輒肆讒毀，動得罪譴，無以自明。

translations.literal: Occasionally there are those upright and strong who keep themselves pure and do not curry favor; they are then slandered at will, often punished and censured, with no way to clear themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Occasionally an official who is upright and refuses to flatter is slandered at will, punished and censured with no way to clear his name.

sentences.zh: 是以使者所至，有司公行貨賂，剝下媚上，有同交易。

translations.literal: Therefore wherever envoys arrive, officials openly practice bribery, stripping those below to please those above, like a trade.
translations.idiomatic: Thus wherever envoys go, officials openly take bribes, squeezing those below to please those above, as if conducting a business deal.

sentences.zh: 夫小民所積幾何，而內外上下誅求如此。

translations.literal: How much can the common people accumulate, when inside and outside, high and low, demand and exact like this?
translations.idiomatic: How much can ordinary people possibly save, when demands from every level of government are so relentless?

sentences.zh: 今山東、河南、山西、陜西水旱相仍，民至剝樹皮掘草根以食。

translations.literal: Now in Shandong, Henan, Shanxi, and Shaanxi flood and drought follow one upon another; the people have reached the point of stripping tree bark and digging grass roots to eat.
translations.idiomatic: In Shandong, Henan, Shanxi, and Shaanxi, flood and drought follow one after another; people have been reduced to stripping tree bark and digging up grass roots for food.

sentences.zh: 老幼流移，顛踣道路，賣妻鬻子以求茍活。

translations.literal: Old and young wander away, falling by the roads; they sell wives and children to seek bare survival.
translations.idiomatic: Old and young wander the roads, collapsing along the way; families sell wives and children just to stay alive.

sentences.zh: 而京師聚集僧道萬餘人，日耗廩米百餘石，此奪民食以養無用也。

translations.literal: Yet in the capital more than ten thousand monks and Daoists are gathered, consuming over a hundred piculs of granary rice daily—this is taking the people's food to nourish the useless.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the capital more than ten thousand monks and Daoist priests are gathered, consuming over a hundred piculs of granary rice each day—this is taking food from the people to sustain the useless.

sentences.zh: 至報效軍士，朝廷厚與糧賜。

translations.literal: As for soldiers who have rendered meritorious service, the court generously grants grain and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: As for soldiers who have rendered meritorious service, the court grants them generous rations and rewards.

sentences.zh: 及使就役，乃驕傲橫恣，閑遊往來。

translations.literal: When they are sent to take up duty, they are arrogant and overbearing, idling and wandering to and fro.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when they are put to work, they grow arrogant and overbearing, idling and roaming about.

sentences.zh: 此皆奸詭之人，懼還原伍，假此規避，非真有報效之心也。

translations.literal: These are all crafty men who fear returning to their original units and use this to evade service; they do not truly have a heart to render merit.
translations.idiomatic: These are all cunning men who fear returning to their original units and use this status to evade duty; they have no real wish to serve.

sentences.zh: 朝廷歲令天下織錦、鑄錢，遣內官買馬外蕃，所出常數千萬，而所取曾不能一二。

translations.literal: Each year the court orders the realm to weave brocade and cast coin, and sends inner eunuchs to buy horses from foreign lands; what is spent commonly runs to tens of millions, yet what is obtained scarcely amounts to one or two parts in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the court orders brocade woven and coin cast throughout the realm, and sends palace eunuchs abroad to buy horses; expenditures routinely run to tens of millions, yet what is obtained scarcely amounts to a tenth.

sentences.zh: 馬至雖多，類皆駑下。

translations.literal: Though many horses arrive, they are mostly inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Though many horses arrive, most are poor stock.

sentences.zh: 責民牧養，騷擾殊甚。

translations.literal: The people are charged to pasture them, and the harassment is extreme.
translations.idiomatic: The people are made to pasture them, and the harassment is severe.

sentences.zh: 及至死傷，輒令賠補。

translations.literal: When they die or are injured, the people are ordered to make compensation.
translations.idiomatic: When horses die or are injured, the people are ordered to make good the loss.

sentences.zh: 馬戶貧困，更鬻妻子。

translations.literal: Horse-keeping households are impoverished and must further sell wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Horse-keeping households are driven to poverty and must sell their wives and children.

sentences.zh: 此尤害之大者。

translations.literal: This is among the greatest harms.
translations.idiomatic: This is among the gravest abuses.

sentences.zh: 漠北降人，賜居室，盛供帳，意欲招其同類也。

translations.literal: For those who surrendered from beyond the northern deserts, dwellings were granted and lavish provisions supplied, intending to attract their kind.
translations.idiomatic: For those who surrendered from beyond the northern deserts, dwellings were granted and lavish provisions supplied, in hopes of attracting others of their kind.

sentences.zh: 不知來者皆懷窺覘，非真遠慕王化，甘去鄉士。

translations.literal: They do not know that those who come all harbor designs of reconnaissance and are not truly drawn from afar by royal transformation, willing to leave their native soil.
translations.idiomatic: They do not realize that those who come are scouting our weaknesses, not truly drawn by civilization or willing to leave their homelands.

sentences.zh: 宜求來朝之後，遣歸本國，不必留為後日子孫患。

translations.literal: After they have come to court, they should be sent back to their own countries and need not be kept to become a trouble for later generations.
translations.idiomatic: After they have paid court, they should be sent back to their own countries rather than kept on to become a trouble for future generations.

sentences.zh: 至宮觀禱祠之事，有國者所當深戒。

translations.literal: As for palace shrines and prayer sacrifices, one who holds a state ought to take deep warning.
translations.idiomatic: As for palace shrines and prayer sacrifices, a ruler should take the deepest warning.

sentences.zh: 古人有言，淫祀無福。

translations.literal: The ancients said that excessive sacrifices bring no blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said that improper sacrifices bring no blessing.

sentences.zh: 況事無益以害有益，蠹財妄費者乎！

translations.literal: How much more when the affair is without benefit yet harms what is beneficial, squandering wealth in vain expense!
translations.idiomatic: How much more when the practice does no good yet harms what is good, squandering wealth in vain!

sentences.zh: 凡此數事，皆下失民心，上違天意。

translations.literal: All these several matters are such that below the people's hearts are lost, and above Heaven's intent is violated.
translations.idiomatic: All these matters alike have lost the people's hearts below and violated Heaven's intent above.

sentences.zh: 怨讟之興，實由於此。

translations.literal: The rise of resentment and complaint truly stems from this.
translations.idiomatic: The rise of resentment and complaint truly stems from this.

sentences.zh: 夫奉天殿者，所以朝群臣，發號令，古所謂明堂也。

translations.literal: The Hall of Imperial Heaven is where ministers are received in audience and orders issued—it is what the ancients called the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Hall of Imperial Heaven is where ministers are received and edicts issued—the ancient Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 而災首及焉，非常之變也。

translations.literal: Yet disaster struck it first—an extraordinary change.
translations.idiomatic: Yet disaster struck it first—an extraordinary omen.

sentences.zh: 非省躬責己，大布恩澤，改革政化，疏滌天下窮困之人，不能回上天譴怒。

translations.literal: Unless Your Majesty examines yourself and blames yourself, broadly dispenses favor, reforms government and transformation, and clears away the destitute of all under Heaven, you cannot turn back Heaven's wrath and reproof.
translations.idiomatic: Unless Your Majesty examines yourself, extends great mercy, reforms policy, and relieves the destitute throughout the realm, you cannot turn aside Heaven's wrath.

sentences.zh: 前有監生生員，以單丁告乞侍親，因而獲罪遣戍者，此實有虧治體。

translations.literal: Earlier there were supervising-student licentiates who, as sole sons, petitioned to attend their parents and for this were punished and sent to frontier garrison—this truly mars the body of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, supervising students who, as sole sons, petitioned to care for their parents were punished and sent to frontier garrison—this truly mars good governance.

sentences.zh: 近者大赦，法司執滯常條，當赦者尚復拘系。

translations.literal: Recently at a great amnesty, the judicial offices clung to routine statutes; those who should have been pardoned were still detained.
translations.idiomatic: At the recent great amnesty, the judicial offices clung to routine statutes, and those who should have been pardoned remained in custody.

sentences.zh: 並乞重加湔洗，蠲除租賦，一切勿征。

translations.literal: I beg that all be thoroughly cleansed anew, rents and levies remitted, and nothing levied at all.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that all these wrongs be thoroughly redressed, rents and levies remitted, and all exactions halted.

sentences.zh: 有司百官全其廩祿，拔簡賢才，申行薦舉，官吏貪贓蠹政者，核其罪而罷黜之。

translations.literal: Let officials and the hundred offices keep their full salaries; select out the worthy; carry out recommendations; and for officials guilty of greed, bribery, and corrupting government, verify their crimes and dismiss them.
translations.idiomatic: Let officials keep their full salaries, select the worthy, carry out recommendations, and for officials guilty of corruption, verify their crimes and dismiss them.

sentences.zh: 則人心歡悅，和氣可臻，所以保安宗社，為國家千萬年無窮之基，莫有大於此者矣。

translations.literal: Then people's hearts will rejoice, harmonious qi can be attained, and thus the ancestral altars can be secured—there is nothing greater than this for the state's foundation of ten thousand years without end.
translations.idiomatic: Then hearts will rejoice, harmony will prevail, and the ancestral altars will be secured—there is no greater foundation for the state's endurance through ten thousand years.

sentences.zh: 且國家所恃以久長者，惟天命人心，而天命常視人心為去留。

translations.literal: Moreover, what the state relies on for long endurance is only the Mandate of Heaven and the people's hearts, and the Mandate of Heaven constantly regards the people's hearts for staying or departing.
translations.idiomatic: What the state relies on for long endurance is the Mandate of Heaven and the people's hearts, and Heaven's Mandate follows where the people's hearts lead.

sentences.zh: 今天意如此，不宜勞民。

translations.literal: Now Heaven's intent is thus; the people ought not to be burdened.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's intent is clear; the people should not be burdened further.

sentences.zh: 當還都南京，奉謁陵廟，告以災變之故。

translations.literal: You should return the capital to Nanjing, pay reverence at the imperial tombs, and report the cause of the calamitous change.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should return the capital to Nanjing, pay reverence at the imperial tombs, and report the cause of this disaster.

sentences.zh: 保養聖躬休息於無為。

translations.literal: Nurture the sage person and rest in non-action.
translations.idiomatic: Nurture your sacred person and rest in quiet governance.

sentences.zh: 毋聽小人之言，復有所興作，以誤陛下於後也。

translations.literal: Do not heed petty men's words and again undertake works, lest you mislead Your Majesty hereafter.
translations.idiomatic: Do not heed petty men's counsel and launch new projects, lest Your Majesty be led astray hereafter.

sentences.zh: 書奏，不省。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; it was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, but the emperor paid it no heed.

sentences.zh: 時三殿初成，帝方以定都詔天下，忽罹火災，頗懼，下詔求直言。

translations.literal: At the time the three halls had just been completed; the emperor had just proclaimed to all under Heaven the fixing of the capital, when suddenly fire disaster struck; he was quite afraid and issued an edict seeking forthright counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The three main halls had just been completed; the emperor had just proclaimed the fixing of the capital to the realm when fire suddenly broke out. Deeply alarmed, he issued an edict calling for frank counsel.

sentences.zh: 及言者多斥時政，帝不懌，而大臣復希旨詆言者。

translations.literal: When many who spoke denounced current policy, the emperor was displeased, and great ministers again followed his intent to slander those who spoke.
translations.idiomatic: When many memorials criticized current policy, the emperor was displeased, and senior ministers again followed his mood to denounce the critics.

sentences.zh: 帝於是發怒，謂言事者謗訕，下詔嚴禁之，犯者不赦。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon grew angry, saying that those who spoke on affairs were slandering, and issued an edict strictly forbidding it; offenders would not be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then flew into a rage, declaring that critics were slandering the throne, and issued an edict strictly forbidding such speech; offenders would not be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 侍讀李時勉、侍講羅汝敬俱下獄；

translations.literal: Reader-in-Waiting Li Shimian and Reader-in-Waiting Luo Rujing were both imprisoned;
translations.idiomatic: Reader-in-Waiting Li Shimian and Reader-in-Waiting Luo Rujing were both thrown into prison;

sentences.zh: 御史鄭維桓、何忠、羅通、徐容，給事中柯暹俱左官交阯。

translations.literal: Censors Zheng Weiheng, He Zhong, Luo Tong, and Xu Rong, and Supervising Secretary Ke Xian were all demoted and sent to Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Zheng Weiheng, He Zhong, Luo Tong, and Xu Rong, and Supervising Secretary Ke Xian were all demoted and sent to Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 惟緝與主事高公望、庶吉士楊復得無罪。

translations.literal: Only Ji, together with Section Chief Gao Gongwang and Hanlin Bachelor Yang Fu, escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zou Ji, together with Section Chief Gao Gongwang and Hanlin Bachelor Yang Fu, escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，緝進右庶子兼侍講。

translations.literal: That winter Ji was promoted to Right Sub-Reader and concurrent Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Zou Ji was promoted to Right Sub-Reader with concurrent appointment as Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 明年九月卒於官。

translations.literal: The next year, in the ninth month, he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the ninth month, he died in office.

sentences.zh: 緝博極群書，居官勤慎，清操如寒士。

translations.literal: Ji was broadly learned in all books; in office he was diligent and careful, his integrity like that of a poor scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Ji was deeply learned, diligent and careful in office, and lived with the integrity of a poor scholar.

sentences.zh: 子循，宣德中為翰林待詔，請贈父母。

translations.literal: His son Xun, during the Xuande reign, served as Hanlin Attendant Draftsman and petitioned to have honors conferred on his parents.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xun, during the Xuande reign, served as Hanlin Attendant Draftsman and petitioned for posthumous honors for his parents.

sentences.zh: 帝諭吏部曰：「曩皇祖征沙漠，朕守北京，緝在左右，陳說皆正道，良臣也，其予之。」

translations.literal: The emperor instructed the Ministry of Personnel, saying: "Formerly, when the imperial ancestor campaigned in the desert and I guarded Beijing, Ji was at my side; what he set forth was all the correct Way—a good minister. Grant it to him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the Ministry of Personnel: "When my grandfather campaigned in the desert and I guarded Beijing, Zou Ji was at my side; everything he advised was sound—a true minister. Grant his request."

sentences.zh: 鄭維桓，慈溪人。

translations.literal: Zheng Weiheng was a native of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Weiheng came from Cixi.

sentences.zh: 永樂十三年進士。

translations.literal: He was a jinshi in the thirteenth year of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirteenth year of Yongle.

sentences.zh: 出知交阯南清州，卒。

translations.literal: He went out as magistrate of Nanqing Prefecture in Jiaozhi and died there.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Nanqing Prefecture in Jiaozhi, where he died in office.

sentences.zh: 柯暹，池州建德人。

translations.literal: Ke Xian was a native of Jiande in Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ke Xian came from Jiande in Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 由鄉舉出知交阯州。

translations.literal: Through provincial recommendation he went out as magistrate of a prefecture in Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Through provincial recommendation he was appointed magistrate of a prefecture in Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 累官浙江、雲南按察使。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Surveillance Commissioner of Zhejiang and Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to serve as Surveillance Commissioner of Zhejiang and Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 弋謙，代州人。

translations.literal: Yi Qian was a native of Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Qian came from Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 永樂九年進士。

translations.literal: He was a jinshi in the ninth year of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the ninth year of Yongle.

sentences.zh: 除監察御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 出按江西，言事忤旨，貶峽山知縣。

translations.literal: Sent out to inspect Jiangxi, he spoke on affairs contrary to the imperial will and was demoted to magistrate of Xiashan.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting Jiangxi, he spoke against imperial policy and was demoted to magistrate of Xiashan.

sentences.zh: 復坐事免歸。

translations.literal: Again, for an offense he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was later dismissed for another offense and returned home.

sentences.zh: 仁宗在東宮，素知謙骨鯁。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor was in the Eastern Palace, he had long known Qian's unyielding integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Renzong Emperor was crown prince, he had long known of Yi Qian's uncompromising integrity.

sentences.zh: 及嗣位，召為大理少卿。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the throne, Qian was summoned as Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When he succeeded to the throne, Yi Qian was summoned to serve as Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 直陳時政，言官吏貪殘，政事多非洪武之舊，及有司誅求無藝。

translations.literal: He spoke frankly on current policy, saying officials were greedy and cruel, that government affairs largely diverged from Hongwu precedents, and that local offices demanded and exacted without limit.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke frankly on current affairs, denouncing official greed and cruelty, policies that diverged from Hongwu precedents, and limitless exactions by local offices.

sentences.zh: 帝多采納。

translations.literal: The emperor adopted much of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted much of his advice.

sentences.zh: 既復言五事，詞太激，帝乃不懌。

translations.literal: Then he again spoke on five matters; his language was too sharp, and the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When he spoke again on five matters in language too sharp, the emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 尚書呂震、吳中，侍郎吳廷用，大理卿虞謙等因劾謙誣罔，都御史劉觀令眾御史合糾謙。

translations.literal: Ministers Lü Zhen and Wu Zhong, Vice Minister Wu Tingyong, Minister of Justice Yu Qian, and others thereupon impeached Qian for falsehood; Censor-in-Chief Liu Guan ordered the censors jointly to impeach Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers Lü Zhen and Wu Zhong, Vice Minister Wu Tingyong, Minister of Justice Yu Qian, and others impeached Yi Qian for falsehood; Censor-in-Chief Liu Guan ordered the censors to join in impeaching him.

sentences.zh: 帝召楊士奇等言之，士奇對曰：「謙不諳大體，然心感超擢恩，欲圖報耳。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Yang Shiqi and others to speak of it; Shiqi replied, saying: "Qian does not understand the larger pattern, yet in his heart he is moved by the grace of sudden promotion and wishes to repay it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Yang Shiqi and others to discuss the matter; Shiqi replied: "Yi Qian does not grasp the larger picture, yet he is moved by the grace of his sudden promotion and wishes to repay it.

sentences.zh: 主聖則臣直，惟陛下優容之。」

translations.literal: When the ruler is sage, ministers are upright—may Your Majesty only treat him with forbearance."
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler is wise, ministers speak plainly—may Your Majesty treat him with forbearance."

sentences.zh: 帝乃不罪謙。

translations.literal: The emperor then did not punish Qian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then did not punish Yi Qian.

sentences.zh: 然每見謙，詞色甚厲。

translations.literal: Yet whenever he saw Qian, his words and expression were very severe.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever he saw Yi Qian, his manner was very harsh.

sentences.zh: 士奇從容言：「陛下詔求直言，謙言不當，觸怒。

translations.literal: Shiqi said calmly: "Your Majesty issued an edict seeking forthright counsel; Qian's words were improper and provoked anger.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi said gently: "Your Majesty issued an edict calling for frank counsel; Yi Qian spoke improperly and provoked your anger.

sentences.zh: 外廷悚惕，以言為戒。

translations.literal: Outside the court all are fearful and take speech as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Officials outside the court are fearful and now treat speech as dangerous.

sentences.zh: 今四方朝覲之臣皆集闕下，見謙如此，將謂陛下不能容直言。」

translations.literal: Now officials from all quarters who have come to court audience are gathered below the palace; seeing Qian treated thus, they will say Your Majesty cannot tolerate forthright counsel."
translations.idiomatic: Envoys from all quarters are now gathered at court; seeing Yi Qian treated thus, they will conclude that Your Majesty cannot tolerate frank counsel."

sentences.zh: 帝惕然曰：「此固朕不能容，亦呂震輩迎合以益朕過，自今當置之。」

translations.literal: The emperor, startled, said: "This is indeed my inability to tolerate—but Lü Zhen and his ilk also flattered to add to my fault; from now on this should be set aside."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, startled, said: "This is indeed my fault in not tolerating counsel—but Lü Zhen and his ilk also flattered me and made my error worse; from now on I shall set this aside."

sentences.zh: 遂免謙朝參，令專視司事。

translations.literal: He thereupon excused Qian from court attendance and ordered him to attend solely to his office duties.
translations.idiomatic: He then excused Yi Qian from court attendance and ordered him to attend solely to his official duties.

sentences.zh: 未幾，帝以言事者益少，復召士奇曰：「朕怒謙矯激過實耳，朝臣遂月餘無言。

translations.literal: Before long, because those who spoke on affairs grew fewer, the emperor again summoned Shiqi and said: "I was angry that Qian was exaggerated and excessive in what was not factual; court officials then went more than a month without speaking.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, because memorials grew fewer, the emperor again summoned Shiqi and said: "I was angry that Yi Qian exaggerated and went beyond the facts; court officials then went more than a month without speaking.

sentences.zh: 爾語諸臣，白朕心。」

translations.literal: You tell the officials and make clear my heart."
translations.idiomatic: Tell the officials and make my true intentions clear."

sentences.zh: 士奇曰：「臣空言不足信，乞親降璽書。」

translations.literal: Shiqi said: "My empty words are not enough to be believed; I beg that Your Majesty personally issue an imperial letter."
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi said: "My words alone will not be believed; I beg that Your Majesty personally issue an imperial letter."

sentences.zh: 遂令就榻前書敕引過曰：「朕自即位以來，臣民上章以數百計，未嘗不欣然聽納。

translations.literal: He then ordered that at the bedside an edict be written acknowledging fault, saying: "Since I took the throne, subjects and people have submitted memorials numbering in the hundreds, and I have never failed to hear and accept them gladly.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered an edict written at his bedside acknowledging fault: "Since I took the throne, subjects have submitted hundreds of memorials, and I have always received them gladly.

sentences.zh: 茍有不當，不加譴訶，群臣所共知也。

translations.literal: If there was anything improper, I did not add reproof and censure—all the ministers know this.
translations.idiomatic: When counsel was improper, I did not add reproof—all my ministers know this.

sentences.zh: 間者，大理少卿弋謙所言，多非實事，群臣迎合朕意，交章奏其賣直，請置諸法。

translations.literal: Recently, what Vice Minister of Justice Yi Qian spoke was largely not factual; the ministers, flattering my intent, jointly memorialized that he was selling uprightness and asked that he be punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, Vice Minister of Justice Yi Qian spoke largely beyond the facts; ministers, flattering my mood, jointly memorialized that he was posturing for reputation and asked that he be punished.

sentences.zh: 朕皆拒而不聽，但免謙朝參。

translations.literal: I refused all and did not listen, only excusing Qian from court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: I refused them all and only excused Yi Qian from court attendance.

sentences.zh: 而自是以來，言者益少。

translations.literal: Since then, those who speak have grown fewer still.
translations.idiomatic: Since then, memorials have grown even fewer.

sentences.zh: 今自去冬無雪，春亦少雨，陰陽愆和，必有其咎，豈無可言？

translations.literal: Now from last winter there has been no snow, and in spring rain has also been scant; yin and yang are out of harmony—there must be a fault. Is there truly nothing that can be said?
translations.idiomatic: From last winter there has been no snow, and spring has brought little rain; yin and yang are out of harmony—there must be a fault. Surely there is something to be said?

sentences.zh: 而為臣者，懷自全之計，退而默默，何以為忠？

translations.literal: Yet as ministers, cherishing plans for self-preservation, you withdraw and keep silent—how is this loyalty?
translations.idiomatic: Yet as ministers, cherishing plans for self-preservation, you withdraw in silence—how is this loyalty?

sentences.zh: 朕于謙一時不能含容，未嘗不自愧咎。

translations.literal: Toward Qian I could not for a time contain myself, yet I have never failed to feel shame and blame myself.
translations.idiomatic: Toward Yi Qian I could not for a time contain myself, yet I have never ceased to feel ashamed.

sentences.zh: 爾群臣勿以前事為戒，於國家利弊、政令未當者，直言勿諱。

translations.literal: You ministers must not take the former affair as a warning; on what benefits or harms the state, or where government orders are improper, speak frankly without reserve.
translations.idiomatic: You ministers must not take the former affair as a warning; on what benefits or harms the state, or where policy is wrong, speak frankly without reserve.

sentences.zh: 謙朝參如故。」

translations.literal: Qian's court attendance is as before."
translations.idiomatic: Yi Qian's court attendance is restored as before."

sentences.zh: 時中官采木四川，貪橫。

translations.literal: At the time palace eunuchs were procuring timber in Sichuan, greedy and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: At the time palace eunuchs were procuring timber in Sichuan, acting with greed and violence.

sentences.zh: 帝以謙清直，命往治之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Qian was pure and upright, ordered him to go and rectify it.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yi Qian was upright, the emperor ordered him to go and rectify the abuses.

sentences.zh: 擢謙副都御史，賜鈔以行，遂罷采木之役。

translations.literal: Qian was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief, given paper money for the journey, and the timber-procurement labor was thereupon halted.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Qian was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief, given paper money for the journey, and the timber-procurement project was halted.

sentences.zh: 宣德初，交阯右布政戚遜以貪淫黜，命謙往代。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuande, Right Administration Commissioner of Jiaozhi Qi Xun was dismissed for greed and debauchery, and Qian was ordered to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xuande, Right Administration Commissioner of Jiaozhi Qi Xun was dismissed for greed and debauchery, and Yi Qian was ordered to replace him.

sentences.zh: 王通棄交阯，謙亦論死。

translations.literal: When Wang Tong abandoned Jiaozhi, Qian was also sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Tong abandoned Jiaozhi, Yi Qian was also sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 正統初，釋為民。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengtong he was released to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhengtong he was released to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 土木之變，謙布衣走闕下，薦通及寧懋、阮遷等十三人，皆奇才可用。

translations.literal: At the Tumu crisis, Qian, in plain clothes, hurried to the palace gate and recommended Wang Tong, Ning Mao, Ruan Qian, and thirteen others—all extraordinary talents who could be employed.
translations.idiomatic: At the Tumu crisis, Yi Qian, in plain clothes, hurried to the palace and recommended Wang Tong, Ning Mao, Ruan Qian, and thirteen others—all men of exceptional talent.

sentences.zh: 眾議以通副石亨，謙請專任通，事遂寢。

translations.literal: The assembly discussed making Tong deputy to Shi Heng; Qian asked that Tong alone be entrusted, and the matter then lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The court discussed making Wang Tong deputy to Shi Heng; Yi Qian asked that Wang Tong alone be entrusted with command, and the matter lapsed.

sentences.zh: 廷臣以謙負重名，奏留之，亦不報。

translations.literal: Court officials, because Qian bore a weighty reputation, memorialized to retain him, but there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials, valuing Yi Qian's reputation, memorialized to retain him, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 景泰二年復至京，疏薦通等，不納。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingtai he again came to the capital and submitted a memorial recommending Tong and others; it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingtai he again came to the capital and submitted a memorial recommending Wang Tong and the others; it was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 罷歸，未幾卒。

translations.literal: Dismissed and returned home, he died before long.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed and returned home, and died before long.

sentences.zh: 仁宗性寬大，容直言，謙以故得無罪，反責呂震等。

translations.literal: The Renzong Emperor was by nature magnanimous and tolerated forthright speech; Qian for this reason escaped punishment, while Lü Zhen and others were instead blamed.
translations.idiomatic: The Renzong Emperor was magnanimous and tolerated frank speech; Yi Qian for this reason escaped punishment, while Lü Zhen and others were blamed instead.

sentences.zh: 而黃驥言西域事，帝亦誚震而行其言。

translations.literal: When Huang Ji spoke on Western Regions affairs, the emperor also reproved Zhen and carried out his words.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Ji spoke on Western Regions affairs, the emperor also reproved Lü Zhen and carried out Huang Ji's advice.

sentences.zh: 驥，全州人。

translations.literal: Ji was a native of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Ji came from Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，中鄉舉。

translations.literal: During Hongwu he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongwu era he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 為沙縣教諭。

translations.literal: He served as instructor of Shaxian.
translations.idiomatic: He served as instructor of Shaxian.

sentences.zh: 永樂時擢禮科給事中，常三使西域。

translations.literal: During Yongle he was promoted to Supervising Secretary in the Ministry of Rites section and often thrice served as envoy to the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongle he was promoted to Supervising Secretary in the Ministry of Rites and often served as envoy to the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 仁宗初，上疏言：「西域貢使多商人假托，無賴小人投為從者，乘傳役人，運貢物至京師，賞賚優厚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renzong he submitted a memorial saying: "Western Regions tribute envoys are mostly merchants falsely posing; worthless petty men attach themselves as followers, ride relay posts and press men into service, transport tribute goods to the capital, and receive lavish rewards.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Renzong's reign he submitted a memorial saying: "Western Regions tribute envoys are mostly merchants in disguise; worthless men attach themselves as followers, abuse the relay system, transport goods to the capital, and receive lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 番人慕利，貢無虛月，致民失業妨農。

translations.literal: Barbarians covet profit; tribute comes in no month without it, causing the people to lose their occupations and harming agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Foreigners covet profit; tribute missions come almost every month, driving people from their occupations and harming agriculture.

sentences.zh: 比其使還，多賫貨物，車運至百餘輛。

translations.literal: When their envoys return, they carry much goods; carts transport them to more than a hundred loads.
translations.idiomatic: When their envoys return, they carry vast quantities of goods, transported in more than a hundred cartloads.

sentences.zh: 丁男不足，役及婦女。

translations.literal: Adult males are insufficient, and labor extends even to women.
translations.idiomatic: When adult males are insufficient, women are pressed into service.

sentences.zh: 所至辱驛官，鞭夫隸，無敢與較者。

translations.literal: Wherever they arrive they insult post officials and whip laborers; none dare contend with them.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever they go they insult post officials and whip laborers, and none dare resist.

sentences.zh: 乞敕陜西行都司，惟哈密諸國王遣使入貢者，許令來京，止正副使得乘驛馬，陜人庶少蘇。

translations.literal: I beg that the Shaanxi Regional Military Commission be ordered that only when kings of states such as Hami send envoys to offer tribute may they be permitted to come to the capital, and only the chief and deputy envoys may ride relay horses, so that the people of Shaanxi may somewhat recover.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the Shaanxi Regional Military Commission be ordered to admit to the capital only envoys sent by kings such as Hami, and to allow only the chief and deputy envoys relay horses, so that the people of Shaanxi may have some relief.

sentences.zh: 至西域所產，惟馬切邊需，應就給甘肅軍士。

translations.literal: As for what the Western Regions produce, only horses are urgently needed on the frontier and should be supplied on the spot to Gansu soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Of Western Regions products, only horses are urgently needed on the frontier and should be supplied directly to Gansu troops.

sentences.zh: 其碙砂、梧桐、鹼之類，皆無益國用，請一切勿受，則來者自稀，浮費益省。」

translations.literal: Such things as sal ammoniac, parasol trees, and alkali are all without benefit to state use; I ask that all be refused, then comers will naturally grow few and wasteful expense further saved."
translations.idiomatic: Products such as sal ammoniac, parasol wood, and alkali are of no use to the state; I ask that all be refused, so that missions will naturally grow fewer and wasteful expense be reduced."

sentences.zh: 帝以示尚書呂震，且讓之曰：「驥嘗奉使，悉西事。

translations.literal: The emperor showed it to Minister Lü Zhen and also reproved him, saying: "Ji has served as envoy and knows Western affairs thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed it to Minister Lü Zhen and reproved him: "Huang Ji has served as envoy and knows Western affairs thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 卿西人，顧不悉邪？

translations.literal: You are a man of the west—do you not know them thoroughly?
translations.idiomatic: You are from the west yourself—do you not know them thoroughly?

sentences.zh: 驥言是，其即議行。」

translations.literal: Ji's words are correct; deliberate and carry them out at once."
translations.idiomatic: Huang Ji is right; deliberate and carry out his proposals at once."

sentences.zh: 後遷右通政，與李琦、羅汝敬撫諭交阯，不辱命。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Right Commissioner of the Transmission Office; with Li Qi and Luo Rujing he pacified and instructed Jiaozhi and did not disgrace the commission.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to Right Commissioner of the Transmission Office; with Li Qi and Luo Rujing he pacified Jiaozhi and acquitted himself honorably.

sentences.zh: 使還，尋卒。

translations.literal: When the mission returned, he soon died.
translations.idiomatic: After the mission returned, he soon died.

sentences.zh: 黃澤，閩縣人。

translations.literal: Huang Ze was a native of Min County.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Ze came from Min County.

sentences.zh: 永樂十年進士。

translations.literal: He was a jinshi in the tenth year of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the tenth year of Yongle.

sentences.zh: 擢河南左參政。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Administration Vice Commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Administration Vice Commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 南陽多流民，拊循使復業。

translations.literal: In Nanyang there were many displaced persons; he comforted and guided them so they resumed their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: In Nanyang there were many displaced people; he comforted and guided them back to their occupations.

sentences.zh: 嘗率丁役至北京，周恤備至。

translations.literal: Once, leading corvée laborers to Beijing, he showed comprehensive care and sympathy.
translations.idiomatic: Once, leading corvée laborers to Beijing, he showed them every consideration.

sentences.zh: 久之，調湖廣。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was transferred to Huguang.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，入覲，言時政，多見采。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor took the throne, he entered for audience, spoke on current policy, and much was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Renzong Emperor took the throne, he came to court, spoke on current affairs, and much of his advice was adopted.

sentences.zh: 宣宗立，下詔求言。

translations.literal: When the Xuanzong Emperor was established, an edict sought counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xuanzong Emperor came to the throne, he issued an edict calling for counsel.

sentences.zh: 澤上疏言正心、恤民、敬天、納諫、練兵、重農、止貢獻、明賞罰、遠嬖幸、汰冗官十事。

translations.literal: Ze submitted a memorial on ten matters: rectifying the heart, cherishing the people, revering Heaven, accepting remonstrance, drilling troops, valuing agriculture, halting tribute offerings, clarifying rewards and punishments, keeping distant favored intimates, and eliminating redundant officials.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Ze submitted a memorial on ten matters: rectifying the heart, cherishing the people, revering Heaven, accepting remonstrance, drilling troops, valuing agriculture, halting tribute missions, clarifying rewards and punishments, keeping favored intimates at a distance, and eliminating redundant officials.

sentences.zh: 其言遠嬖幸曰：「刑余之人，其情幽陰，其慮險譎。

translations.literal: On keeping distant favored intimates he said: "Those mutilated by punishment—their feelings are hidden and dark, their thoughts treacherous and devious.
translations.idiomatic: On keeping favored intimates at a distance he said: "Those mutilated by punishment have hidden, dark natures and treacherous, devious minds.

sentences.zh: 大奸似忠，大詐似信，大巧似愚。

translations.literal: Great villainy resembles loyalty, great deceit resembles trustworthiness, great craft resembles stupidity.
translations.idiomatic: Great villainy resembles loyalty, great deceit resembles trustworthiness, great craft resembles stupidity.

sentences.zh: 一與之親，如飲醇酒，不知其醉；

translations.literal: Once intimate with them, it is like drinking strong wine without knowing one is drunk;
translations.idiomatic: Once intimate with them, it is like drinking strong wine without knowing one is drunk;

sentences.zh: 如噬甘臘，不知其毒。

translations.literal: like eating sweet cured meat without knowing its poison.
translations.idiomatic: like eating sweet cured meat without knowing its poison.

sentences.zh: 寵之甚易，遠之甚難。

translations.literal: Favoring them is very easy; keeping them distant is very hard.
translations.idiomatic: Favoring them is easy; keeping them at a distance is hard.

sentences.zh: 是以古者宦寺不使典兵幹政，所以防患於未萌也。

translations.literal: Therefore in antiquity eunuchs and palace attendants were not allowed to command troops or meddle in government—this was to guard against trouble before it sprouted.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in antiquity eunuchs were not allowed to command troops or meddle in government—to guard against trouble before it sprouted.

sentences.zh: 涓涓弗塞，將為江河。

translations.literal: A trickle unstopped will become a river.
translations.idiomatic: A trickle unstopped will become a river.

sentences.zh: 此輩宜一切疏遠，勿使用事。

translations.literal: This sort should all be kept distant and not employed in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Such people should all be kept at a distance and not employed in affairs.

sentences.zh: 漢、唐已事，彰彰可監。」

translations.literal: The affairs of Han and Tang are clear warnings to observe."
translations.idiomatic: The histories of Han and Tang offer clear warnings."

sentences.zh: 當成祖時，宦官稍稍用事，宣宗浸以親幸。

translations.literal: During Chengzu's time, eunuchs gradually came into use; the Xuanzong Emperor increasingly favored them intimately.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yongle Emperor, eunuchs gradually gained influence; the Xuanzong Emperor increasingly favored them.

sentences.zh: 澤於十事中此為尤切。

translations.literal: Among Ze's ten matters this was especially pointed.
translations.idiomatic: Among Huang Ze's ten proposals, this was especially pointed.

sentences.zh: 帝雖嘉嘆，不能用也。

translations.literal: Though the emperor praised and sighed over it, he could not employ it.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor praised it, he could not put it into practice.

sentences.zh: 其後設內書堂，而中人多通書曉文義。

translations.literal: Afterward the Inner Calligraphy Hall was established, and many eunuchs mastered books and understood literary meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the Inner Calligraphy Hall was established, and many eunuchs became literate and versed in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 宦寺之盛，自宣宗始。

translations.literal: The flourishing of eunuchs and palace attendants began from Xuanzong.
translations.idiomatic: The rise of eunuch power began with the Xuanzong Emperor.

sentences.zh: 宣德三年擢浙江布政使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuande he was promoted to Administration Commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xuande he was promoted to Administration Commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 復上言平陽、麗水等七縣銀冶宜罷，並請盡罷諸坑冶，語甚切。

translations.literal: He again memorialized that the silver smelteries of the seven counties including Pingyang and Lishui should be halted, and asked that all mining and smelting pits be entirely abolished; his language was very pointed.
translations.idiomatic: He again memorialized that silver smelteries in seven counties including Pingyang and Lishui should be shut down, and asked that all mining operations be abolished; his language was very pointed.

sentences.zh: 帝嘆息曰：「民困若此，朕何由知？

translations.literal: The emperor sighed and said: "The people are in such distress—how am I to know of it?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed and said: "The people are suffering like this—how was I to know?

sentences.zh: 遣官驗視，酌議以聞。」

translations.literal: Send officials to inspect and verify, deliberate on measures, and report."
translations.idiomatic: Send officials to inspect the situation, work out appropriate measures, and report back to me."

sentences.zh: 澤在官有政績，然多暴怒，鹽運使丁鎡不避道，撻之，為所奏。

translations.literal: While in office Ze had administrative achievements, yet he was often violently angry; the salt-transport commissioner Ding Zeng did not yield the road, and Ze beat him—whereupon Ding memorialized against him.
translations.idiomatic: While in office Huang Ze had real achievements, yet he was prone to violent rage; when the salt-transport commissioner Ding Zeng failed to yield the road, Ze beat him, and Ding memorialized against him.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史馬謹亦劾澤九載秩滿，自出行縣，斂白金三千兩償官物，且越境過家。

translations.literal: The regional inspecting censor Ma Jin also impeached Ze, saying that at the end of his nine-year term he went out on his own to tour the counties, collected three thousand taels of white silver to pay for official goods, and moreover crossed the border to visit home.
translations.idiomatic: The regional inspecting censor Ma Jin also impeached Huang Ze, charging that when his nine-year term expired he toured the counties on his own authority, collected three thousand taels of silver to cover official expenses, and crossed his jurisdiction to visit home.

sentences.zh: 遂逮下獄。

translations.literal: He was then arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was then arrested and thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 正統六年黜為民。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengtong he was dismissed and reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhengtong he was dismissed and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 初，澤奏金華、臺州戶口較洪武時耗減，而歲造弓箭如舊，乞減免。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ze had memorialized that the household registers of Jinhua and Taizhou had declined compared with Hongwu times, yet annual manufacture of bows and arrows remained as before, and he asked for reduction and exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Huang Ze had memorialized that household registers in Jinhua and Taizhou had fallen since the Hongwu era, while the annual quota for bows and arrows remained unchanged, and he asked that the levy be reduced.

sentences.zh: 下部議得允，而澤已罷官逾月矣。

translations.literal: The matter was sent to the ministry for deliberation and approval was granted, but Ze had already been removed from office for more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry deliberated and approved the request, but Huang Ze had already been out of office for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 孔友諒，長洲人。

translations.literal: Kong Youliang was a native of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Youliang came from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 永樂十六年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the sixteenth year of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the sixteenth year of Yongle.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，出知雙流縣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin Bachelor and then sent out as magistrate of Shuangliu County.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a Hanlin Bachelor, then sent out to serve as magistrate of Shuangliu County.

sentences.zh: 宣宗初，上言六事：

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuanzong he submitted a memorial on six matters:
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xuanzong reign he submitted a memorial on six matters:

sentences.zh: 一曰，守令親民之官，古者不拘資格，必得其人；

translations.literal: First: prefects and magistrates are officials close to the people; in antiquity qualifications were not rigidly fixed—the right person had to be obtained;
translations.idiomatic: First: prefects and magistrates are the officials closest to the people; in antiquity appointments were not bound by seniority—the right person had to be found;

sentences.zh: 不限歲月，使盡其力。

translations.literal: years in office were not limited, so that they could exert their full strength.
translations.idiomatic: and terms of office were not fixed, so that they could give their full effort.

sentences.zh: 今居職者多不知撫字之方，而廉幹得民心者，又遷調不常，差遣不一。

translations.literal: Today most in office do not know the methods of governing and nurturing the people, while those who are upright, capable, and win the people's hearts are transferred and reassigned without regularity, with assignments inconsistent.
translations.idiomatic: Today most local officials do not know how to govern and care for the people, while those who are honest, capable, and win popular trust are transferred constantly and sent on one assignment after another.

sentences.zh: 或因小事連累，朝夕營治，往來道路，日不暇給。

translations.literal: Some are implicated over minor matters, scheming morning and evening, traveling back and forth on the roads, with days never sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Some are dragged into trouble over minor matters, scrambling day and night, constantly on the road, with never a moment to spare.

sentences.zh: 乞敕吏部，擇才望素優及久歷京官者任之。

translations.literal: I beg that the Ministry of Personnel be ordered to select those of consistently superior talent and reputation, and those long experienced in capital office, to fill these posts.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the Ministry of Personnel be ordered to appoint men of proven talent and reputation, and those with long experience in capital office.

sentences.zh: 諭戒上司，毋擅差遣，假以歲月，責成治效。

translations.literal: Superiors should be instructed and warned not to dispatch them at will; grant them time, and hold them accountable for results in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Their superiors should be instructed not to reassign them at will, given adequate time in post, and held accountable for results.

sentences.zh: 至遠缺佐貳，多經裁減，獨員居職。

translations.literal: As for distant posts and assistant officials, many have been cut by retrenchment, leaving a single official in charge.
translations.idiomatic: As for distant posts and their deputies, many positions have been cut, leaving a single official in charge.

sentences.zh: 或遇事赴京，多委雜職署事，因循茍且，政令無常，民不知畏。

translations.literal: When affairs arise some go to the capital, and many matters are entrusted to miscellaneous officials to handle in their stead; they muddle through perfunctorily, government orders are erratic, and the people know not what to fear.
translations.idiomatic: When business arises some officials go to the capital, leaving affairs to minor substitutes who muddle through; policies shift constantly and the people no longer know what to respect.

sentences.zh: 今後路遠之缺，常留一正員任事，不得擅離，庶法有常守。

translations.literal: Henceforth for distant posts one regular official should always remain on duty and may not leave without authorization, so that the law may have constant observance.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth at distant posts one regular official should always remain on duty and not leave without authorization, so that governance may be steady and predictable.

sentences.zh: 二曰，科舉所以求賢，必名實相副，非徒誇多而已。

translations.literal: Second: the civil examinations exist to seek the worthy; name and reality must correspond—it is not merely to boast of numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Second: the civil examinations exist to find worthy men; credentials and ability must match—it is not merely a matter of filling quotas.

sentences.zh: 今秋闈取士動一二百人。

translations.literal: Today the provincial examinations take one or two hundred candidates at a stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Today the provincial examinations routinely pass one or two hundred candidates at a time.

sentences.zh: 弊既多端，僥幸過半。

translations.literal: Abuses are already manifold, and more than half pass by luck.
translations.idiomatic: Abuses are already manifold, and more than half succeed by luck alone.

sentences.zh: 會試下第，十常八九，其登第者，實行或乖。

translations.literal: At the metropolitan examination most fail—eight or nine out of ten—and among those who pass, conduct often falls short.
translations.idiomatic: At the metropolitan examination eight or nine out of ten fail, and even among those who pass, conduct often falls short.

sentences.zh: 請於開科之歲，詳核諸生行履。

translations.literal: I ask that in years when examinations are held, the conduct and records of students be thoroughly verified.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that in years when examinations are held, the conduct and records of candidates be thoroughly verified.

sentences.zh: 孝弟忠信、學業優贍者，乃許入試。

translations.literal: Only those filial, fraternal, loyal, and trustworthy, with superior and ample learning, should be permitted to enter the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Only those who are filial, loyal, trustworthy, and solidly educated should be allowed to sit for the exams.

sentences.zh: 庶浮薄不致濫收，而國家得真才之用。

translations.literal: Thus the frivolous and shallow will not be indiscriminately admitted, and the state will obtain the use of true talent.
translations.idiomatic: Then the frivolous will not slip through, and the state will gain men of real ability.

sentences.zh: 三曰，祿以養廉，祿入過薄，則生事不給。

translations.literal: Third: salary exists to nurture integrity; when salary income is too thin, life's affairs cannot be supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Third: salaries exist to sustain integrity; when pay is too meager, officials cannot meet the demands of daily life.

sentences.zh: 國朝制祿之典，視前代為薄。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's system of fixed salaries is thinner than that of previous ages.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty's salary scale is thinner than that of previous dynasties.

sentences.zh: 今京官及方面官稍增俸祿，其餘大小官自折鈔外，月不過米二石，不足食數人。

translations.literal: Today capital officials and regional officials have had salaries slightly increased, but for the rest, large and small officials aside from paper-money conversion receive no more than two shi of grain per month—not enough to feed several people.
translations.idiomatic: Capital officials and regional commissioners have received modest raises, but for most other officials, apart from paper-money conversion, monthly pay is no more than two shi of grain—not enough to feed a household.

sentences.zh: 仰事俯育，與道路往來，費安所取資？

translations.literal: Serving those above and nurturing those below, and traveling on the roads—whence are expenses to be drawn?
translations.idiomatic: Supporting parents, raising children, and traveling on official business—where is the money to come from?

sentences.zh: 貪者放利行私，廉者終窶莫訴。

translations.literal: The greedy pursue profit and act for private ends; the upright end in poverty with no one to whom to appeal.
translations.idiomatic: The greedy turn to profit and private gain; the honest end in poverty with no recourse.

sentences.zh: 請敕戶部勘實天下糧儲，以歲支之余，量增官俸。

translations.literal: I ask that the Ministry of Revenue be ordered to verify the empire's grain stores, and from the surplus of annual expenditure incrementally increase official salaries.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the Ministry of Revenue verify the empire's grain reserves and use the annual surplus to increase official salaries proportionally.

sentences.zh: 仍令內外風憲官，采訪廉潔之吏，重加旌賞。

translations.literal: Moreover, let censorial officials within and without be ordered to seek out upright and clean officials and reward them heavily.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials at court and in the provinces should also be ordered to seek out honest officials and reward them generously.

sentences.zh: 則廉者知勸，貪者知戒。

translations.literal: Then the upright will know encouragement, and the greedy will know warning.
translations.idiomatic: Then the honest will be encouraged, and the corrupt will take warning.

sentences.zh: 四曰，古者賦役量土宜，驗丁口，不責所無，不盡所有。

translations.literal: Fourth: in antiquity tax and corvée were measured to local conditions, verified against household registers, not demanding what was lacking, not exhausting what was possessed.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: in antiquity taxes and corvée were set according to local conditions and household registers, demanding neither what people lacked nor everything they had.

sentences.zh: 今自常賦外，復有和買、采辦諸事。

translations.literal: Today beyond the regular levies there are again government procurement, court requisition, and other such matters.
translations.idiomatic: Today, beyond regular taxes, there are government procurement, court requisitions, and other such exactions.

sentences.zh: 自朝廷視之，不過令有司支官錢平買。

translations.literal: From the court's perspective, it is merely ordering local officials to disburse official funds and buy at fair price.
translations.idiomatic: From the court's perspective, these are merely orders for local officials to pay official funds and buy goods at fair prices.

sentences.zh: 而無賴之輩，關通吏胥，壟斷貨物，巧立辨驗、折耗之名，科取數倍，奸弊百端。

translations.literal: Yet worthless fellows collude with clerks and runners, monopolize goods, and artfully establish names such as inspection fees and wastage deductions, levying several times the amount—corruption in every form.
translations.idiomatic: Yet ruffians collude with clerks, monopolize goods, and invent fees for inspection and wastage, extracting several times the proper amount—corruption in every form.

sentences.zh: 乞盡停采買，減諸不急務，則國賦有常，民無科擾。

translations.literal: I beg that court requisitions be entirely halted and non-urgent matters reduced; then state levies will be regular and the people free from exactions and harassment.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that court requisitions be halted entirely and nonessential demands reduced, so that state levies remain stable and the people are spared harassment.

sentences.zh: 其二事言汰冗員，任風憲，言者多及之，不具載。

translations.literal: The other two matters spoke of eliminating redundant posts and entrusting censorial authority; many memorials touched on these and they are not fully recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: The other two proposals concerned eliminating redundant posts and strengthening censorial authority; many memorials touched on these topics and they are not recorded in full here.

sentences.zh: 宣德八年，命吏部擇外官有文學者六十八人試之，得友諒及進士胡端禎等七人，悉令辦事六科。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xuande the Ministry of Personnel was ordered to select sixty-eight local officials with literary attainment for examination; seven were chosen, including Youliang and the jinshi Hu Duanzhen, and all were ordered to serve in the Six Offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Xuande the Ministry of Personnel was ordered to test sixty-eight local officials of literary attainment; seven passed, including Kong Youliang and the jinshi Hu Duanzhen, and all were assigned to the Six Offices.

sentences.zh: 居二年，皆授給事中，惟友諒未授官而卒。

translations.literal: After two years all were appointed supervising secretaries; only Youliang died before receiving appointment.
translations.idiomatic: After two years all were appointed supervising secretaries; only Kong Youliang died before he could take up his post.

sentences.zh: 範濟，元進士。

translations.literal: Fan Ji was a Yuan-dynasty jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ji had passed the jinshi examination under the Yuan.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，以文學舉為廣信知府，坐累謫戍興州。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu era he was recommended for literary attainment and appointed prefect of Guangxin; implicated in a case, he was demoted and sent to garrison duty at Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hongwu era he was recommended for his learning and appointed prefect of Guangxin; implicated in a case, he was demoted and sent to garrison duty at Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，濟年八十餘矣，詣闕言八事：

translations.literal: When Xuanzong took the throne, Ji was already more than eighty years old; he came to the court and spoke on eight matters:
translations.idiomatic: When the Xuanzong Emperor took the throne, Fan Ji was already over eighty; he came to court and submitted a memorial on eight matters:

sentences.zh: 其一曰楮幣之法，昉於漢、唐。

translations.literal: The first concerned the method of paper currency, which began in Han and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: The first concerned paper currency, a practice that began in the Han and Tang dynasties.

sentences.zh: 元造元統交鈔，後又造中統鈔。

translations.literal: The Yuan minted Yuantong exchange notes, and afterward also minted Zhongtong notes.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan issued Yuantong exchange notes, and later Zhongtong notes as well.

sentences.zh: 久而物重鈔輕，公私俱敝，乃造至元鈔與中統鈔兼行。

translations.literal: Over time goods grew heavy and notes light; public and private alike were exhausted, so Zhiyuan notes were minted to circulate jointly with Zhongtong notes.
translations.idiomatic: Over time goods appreciated and notes depreciated, exhausting both public and private resources, so Zhiyuan notes were issued to circulate alongside Zhongtong notes.

sentences.zh: 子母相權，新陳通用。

translations.literal: Parent and child notes were mutually weighted; new and old were used in common.
translations.idiomatic: Old and new notes were weighted against each other, and both circulated freely.

sentences.zh: 又令民間以昏鈔赴平準庫，中統鈔五貫得換至元鈔一貫。

translations.literal: The people were also ordered to bring worn notes to the stabilization treasury; five strings of Zhongtong notes could be exchanged for one string of Zhiyuan notes.
translations.idiomatic: The people were also allowed to bring worn notes to the stabilization treasury and exchange five strings of Zhongtong notes for one string of Zhiyuan notes.

sentences.zh: 又其法日造萬錠，共計官吏俸稍、內府供用若干，天下正稅雜課若干，斂發有方，周流不滯，以故久而通行。

translations.literal: Moreover, the method called for ten thousand ingots to be minted daily; the amounts for official salaries, inner-palace supplies, regular taxes, and miscellaneous levies were all calculated; collection and disbursement had fixed methods, circulation was unimpeded, and for this reason the system endured and remained in use.
translations.idiomatic: The system also called for ten thousand ingots to be minted daily, with fixed amounts set aside for official salaries, palace supplies, regular taxes, and miscellaneous levies; collection and disbursement were regulated, circulation was smooth, and for this reason the currency remained viable for a long time.

sentences.zh: 太祖皇帝造大明寶鈔。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor created the Great Ming treasure notes.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwu Emperor created the Great Ming treasure notes.

sentences.zh: 以鈔一貫當白金一兩，民歡趨之。

translations.literal: One string of notes was equivalent to one tael of white silver, and the people gladly rushed to use them.
translations.idiomatic: One string of notes was set equal to one tael of silver, and the people readily accepted them.

sentences.zh: 迄今五十餘年，其法稍弊，亦由物重鈔輕所致。

translations.literal: To the present, more than fifty years on, the method has somewhat decayed—also because goods grew heavy and notes light.
translations.idiomatic: More than fifty years later the system has begun to fail, again because goods have appreciated while notes have depreciated.

sentences.zh: 願陛下因時變通，重造寶鈔，一準洪武初制，使新舊兼行。

translations.literal: I wish that Your Majesty, adapting to the times, remint treasure notes according exactly to the early Hongwu system, so that new and old circulate jointly.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty adapt to the times, remint treasure notes according to the early Hongwu standard, and let new and old notes circulate together.

sentences.zh: 取元時所造之數而增損之，審國家度支之數而權衡之。

translations.literal: Take the quantities minted in Yuan times and increase or reduce them; examine the state's expenditure figures and weigh them accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Adjust the quantities minted under the Yuan, and calibrate them against the state's actual expenditure.

sentences.zh: 俾鈔少而物多，鈔重而物輕。

translations.literal: Thus notes will be few and goods many; notes heavy and goods light.
translations.idiomatic: So that notes are scarce and goods plentiful, notes strong and goods cheap.

sentences.zh: 嚴偽造之條，開倒換之法，推陳出新，無耗無阻，則鈔法流通，永永無弊。

translations.literal: Strictly enforce penalties for counterfeiting, open methods of exchange, push out the old and bring in the new without loss or obstruction—then the note system will circulate and forever be without defect.
translations.idiomatic: Strictly punish counterfeiting, establish exchange procedures, retire old notes and issue new ones without loss or obstruction—and the currency will circulate soundly for the long term.

sentences.zh: 其二曰備邊之道，守險為要。

translations.literal: The second concerned border defense: holding strategic terrain is essential.
translations.idiomatic: The second concerned border defense: holding strategic terrain is the key.

sentences.zh: 若朔州、大同、開平、宣府、大寧，乃京師之藩垣，邊僥之門戶。

translations.literal: Such places as Shuozhou, Datong, Kaiping, Xuanfu, and Daining are the protective walls of the capital and the gateways of the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Places such as Shuozhou, Datong, Kaiping, Xuanfu, and Daining are the protective walls of the capital and the gateways to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 士可耕，城可守。

translations.literal: The land can be farmed and the cities defended.
translations.idiomatic: The land can be farmed and the fortresses held.

sentences.zh: 宜盛兵防禦，廣開屯田，修治城堡，謹烽火，明斥堠。

translations.literal: Troops should be massed for defense, garrison farming broadly opened, fortresses repaired, beacon fires maintained with care, and sentry posts clearly manned.
translations.idiomatic: Troops should be concentrated for defense, garrison farming expanded, fortresses repaired, beacon fires maintained vigilantly, and sentry posts clearly manned.

sentences.zh: 毋貪小利，毋輕遠求，堅壁清野，使無所得。

translations.literal: Do not covet small gains, do not lightly pursue distant objectives; strengthen walls and clear the countryside so that the enemy gains nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Do not chase small gains or rash distant campaigns; strengthen the walls, clear the countryside, and leave the enemy with nothing to seize.

sentences.zh: 俟其憊而擊之，得利則止，毋窮追深入。

translations.literal: Wait until they are exhausted and then strike; when advantage is gained, stop—do not pursue to exhaustion and penetrate deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until they are exhausted, then strike; when you have gained an advantage, stop—do not pursue them deep into their territory.

sentences.zh: 此守邊大要也。

translations.literal: These are the great essentials of guarding the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: These are the essential principles of frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 其三曰兵不在多，在於堪戰。

translations.literal: The third: troops lie not in numbers but in being fit for battle.
translations.idiomatic: The third: armies are measured not by numbers but by fighting ability.

sentences.zh: 比者多發為事官吏人民充軍塞上，非白面書生，則老弱病廢。

translations.literal: Recently many officials and common people implicated in cases have been dispatched to fill garrison ranks on the frontier—if not pale-faced bookish scholars, then the old, weak, sick, and disabled.
translations.idiomatic: Recently many officials and commoners implicated in legal cases have been sent to fill garrison ranks on the frontier—if not bookish scholars, then the old, weak, sick, and disabled.

sentences.zh: 遇有征行，有力者得免，貧弱者備數。

translations.literal: When campaigns arise, the strong and well-connected are exempted, while the poor and weak make up the numbers.
translations.idiomatic: When campaigns arise, the strong and well-connected buy their way out, while the poor and weak merely fill the rolls.

sentences.zh: 器械不完，糗糧不具。

translations.literal: Weapons and equipment are incomplete; rations and provisions are not supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Weapons are incomplete and rations not provided.

sentences.zh: 望風股栗，安能效死？

translations.literal: At the sight of the enemy their thighs tremble—how can they fight to the death?
translations.idiomatic: They tremble at the sight of the enemy—how can they be expected to fight to the death?

sentences.zh: 今宜選其壯勇，勤加訓練，余但令乘城擊柝，趨走牙門，庶幾各得其用。

translations.literal: Now the strong and brave should be selected and diligently trained; the rest should merely be ordered to man the walls, beat the night watches, and run errands at headquarters—then each may nearly find his proper use.
translations.idiomatic: The strong and brave should be selected and rigorously trained; the rest should be assigned to wall duty, night watches, and camp errands, so that each man serves where he is fit.

sentences.zh: 其四曰民病莫甚於勾軍。

translations.literal: The fourth: among the people's afflictions none is worse than conscription rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth: among the people's afflictions none is worse than the conscription rolls.

sentences.zh: 衛所差官至六七員，百戶差軍旗亦二三人，皆有力交結及畏避征調之徒，重賄得遣。

translations.literal: Guard units dispatch as many as six or seven officials; company commanders also send two or three military runners—all men with powerful connections or those who fear and evade mobilization, who obtain dispatch through heavy bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Guard units dispatch as many as six or seven officials, and company commanders send two or three military runners as well—all men with powerful connections or those seeking to evade mobilization, who secure the assignment through heavy bribes.

sentences.zh: 既至州縣，擅作威福，迫脅裏甲，恣為奸私。

translations.literal: Once they reach prefectures and counties they arrogantly wield power, coerce community heads, and indulge in private corruption as they please.
translations.idiomatic: Once they reach the counties they abuse their authority, coerce community heads, and indulge in private corruption.

sentences.zh: 無丁之家，誅求不已；

translations.literal: From households with no eligible men, extortion never ceases;
translations.idiomatic: From households with no eligible men, extortion never ceases;

sentences.zh: 有丁之戶，詐稱死亡。

translations.literal: households with eligible men falsely claim death.
translations.idiomatic: households with eligible men falsely report deaths.

sentences.zh: 托故留滯，久而不還。

translations.literal: Finding pretexts they linger and do not return for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: They invent excuses to linger and do not return for a long time.

sentences.zh: 及還，則以所得財物，遍賄官吏，朦朧具覆。

translations.literal: When they return, they use the goods obtained to bribe officials throughout, and vaguely submit their reports.
translations.idiomatic: When they return, they use their gains to bribe officials up and down the line and submit vague, misleading reports.

sentences.zh: 究其所取之丁，十不得一，欲軍無缺伍難矣。

translations.literal: Investigating the men they actually obtained, not one in ten is found—how difficult to keep the army without vacant ranks!
translations.idiomatic: In the end not one man in ten is actually obtained—keeping the army at full strength is impossible.

sentences.zh: 自今軍士有故，令各衛報都督府及兵部，府、部諜布政、按察司。

translations.literal: From now on when soldiers suffer vacancies, let each guard report to the regional military commission and the Ministry of War; the commission and ministry shall notify the provincial administration commission and regional inspection commission.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth when soldiers fall vacant, each guard should report to the regional military commission and the Ministry of War, which should notify the provincial administration commission and regional inspection commission.

sentences.zh: 令府州縣準籍貫姓名，勾取送衛，則差人騷擾之弊自絕。

translations.literal: Let prefectures, subprefectures, and counties according to registered native place and name summon and deliver replacements to the guard—then the abuse of dispatching agents and harassment will cease of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties should summon men by registered name and native place and deliver them directly to the guard—then the abuse of dispatching agents and harassing the people will end.

sentences.zh: 其五曰洪武中令軍士七分屯田，三分守城，最為善策。

translations.literal: The fifth: in the Hongwu era soldiers were ordered to farm garrison fields seven parts in ten and guard cities three parts in ten—the finest policy.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth: in the Hongwu era soldiers were ordered to spend seven-tenths of their time on garrison farming and three-tenths on defense—the finest policy of all.

sentences.zh: 比者調度日繁，興造日廣，虛有屯種之名，田多荒蕪。

translations.literal: Recently requisitions grow daily more frequent and construction daily more extensive; the name of garrison planting exists in vain, and fields are largely abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Recently requisitions have grown ever more frequent and construction ever more extensive; garrison farming exists in name only, and fields lie largely abandoned.

sentences.zh: 兼養馬、采草、伐薪、燒炭，雜役旁午，兵力焉得不疲、農業焉得不廢？
