translations.literal: Added to this are horse-rearing, grass-gathering, firewood-cutting, charcoal-burning, and miscellaneous corvée coming from every direction—how can military strength not be exhausted, and agriculture not be ruined?
translations.idiomatic: Added to this are horse-rearing, foraging, firewood-cutting, charcoal-burning, and miscellaneous corvée from every direction—how can the troops not be exhausted and farming not collapse?

sentences.zh: 願敕邊將課卒墾荒，限以頃畝，官給牛種，稽其勤惰，明賞罰以示勸懲。

translations.literal: I wish that frontier generals be ordered to set soldiers to reclaim wasteland, limited by acreage; the state should supply oxen and seed, examine diligence and sloth, and make rewards and punishments clear to show encouragement and warning.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that frontier commanders be ordered to set soldiers to reclaim wasteland within fixed acreage limits, supply oxen and seed, monitor diligence and sloth, and apply clear rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 則塞下田可盡墾，轉餉益紓，諸邊富實，計無便於此者。

translations.literal: Then frontier fields can be fully reclaimed, transport of provisions will be further eased, and the borders will grow rich and solid—no measure is more convenient than this.
translations.idiomatic: Then frontier land can be fully reclaimed, transport costs eased, and the border regions made prosperous—no policy would be more effective.

sentences.zh: 其六曰，學校者，風化之源，人材所自出，貴明體適用，非徒較文藝而已也。

translations.literal: The sixth: schools are the source of moral transformation and the wellspring from which talent emerges; what is valued is clarity of principle and practical fitness—not merely comparing literary skill.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth: schools are the source of moral cultivation and the wellspring of talent; what matters is grasp of principle and practical ability—not literary display alone.

sentences.zh: 洪武中妙選師儒，教養甚備，人材彬彬可觀。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu era teachers and scholars were finely selected, instruction and nurturing were very complete, and talent was abundant and admirable.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hongwu era teachers were carefully chosen, education was thorough, and talent flourished impressively.

sentences.zh: 邇來士習委靡，立志不弘，執節不固。

translations.literal: Recently scholarly habits have been lax; resolve is not broad, and adherence to principle is not firm.
translations.idiomatic: Recently scholarly habits have grown slack; students lack broad ambition and firm adherence to principle.

sentences.zh: 平居無剛方正大之氣，安望其立朝為名公卿哉！

translations.literal: In ordinary life they have no spirit of firmness, rectitude, and magnanimity—how can one expect them to stand at court as renowned ministers and grandees!
translations.idiomatic: In daily life they show no spirit of firmness and integrity—how can we expect them to serve at court as great ministers!

sentences.zh: 宜選良士為郡縣學官，擇民間子弟性行端謹者為生徒，訓以經史，勉以節行。

translations.literal: Worthy men should be selected as county and prefectural school officers; youths from among the people whose character and conduct are upright and careful should be chosen as students, instructed in the classics and histories, and encouraged in integrity of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy men should be chosen as county and prefectural school instructors; upright and careful youths should be selected as students, trained in the classics and histories, and encouraged in moral conduct.

sentences.zh: 俟其有成，貢於國學。

translations.literal: When they have achieved maturity, present them to the National Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When they have matured, send them to the National Academy.

sentences.zh: 磨礱砥礪，使其氣充誌定，卓然成材，然後舉而用之，以任天下國家事無難矣。

translations.literal: Grinding and sharpening them until their spirit is full and their will fixed, they become outstanding talent; then selecting and employing them to undertake the affairs of the empire and the state—nothing will be difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Hone them until their spirit is strong and their purpose fixed; once they have truly matured, appoint them to office, and the affairs of the empire will present no difficulty.

sentences.zh: 其七曰兵者凶器，聖人不得已而用之。

translations.literal: The seventh: arms are ill-omened instruments; the sage employs them only when he has no choice.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh: arms are instruments of violence; the sage uses them only when he has no choice.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖解平城之圍，未聞蕭、曹勸以復仇；

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu of Han broke the siege at Pingcheng, one never heard Xiao or Cao urge revenge;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu of Han broke the siege at Pingcheng, Xiao He and Cao Shen did not urge revenge;

sentences.zh: 唐太宗禦突厥於便橋，未聞房、杜勸以報怨。

translations.literal: when Emperor Taizong of Tang faced the Turks at Bian Bridge, one never heard Fang or Du urge settling old scores.
translations.idiomatic: when Emperor Taizong of Tang faced the Turks at Bian Bridge, Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui did not urge retaliation.

sentences.zh: 古英君良相不欲疲民力以誇武功，計慮遠矣。

translations.literal: Wise rulers and good ministers of old did not wish to exhaust the people's strength to boast of military achievement—their planning was far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Wise rulers and good ministers of old did not exhaust the people's strength to boast of military glory—their vision was long.

sentences.zh: 洪武初年嘗赫然命將，欲清沙漠。

translations.literal: In the early Hongwu era the court once majestically ordered generals forth, wishing to clear the desert.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Hongwu era the court once boldly dispatched generals, intending to pacify the desert.

sentences.zh: 既以饋運不繼，旋即頒師。

translations.literal: Since supply transport could not be sustained, they immediately withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: When supply lines failed, the army was promptly withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 遂撤東勝衛於大同，塞山西陽武谷口，選將練兵，扼險以待。

translations.literal: They then relocated the Dongsheng Guard to Datong, blocked Yangwu Pass in Shanxi, selected generals and drilled troops, and held the strategic passes awaiting the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: They relocated the Dongsheng Guard to Datong, sealed Yangwu Pass in Shanxi, selected generals, trained troops, and held the strategic passes in readiness.

sentences.zh: 內修政教，外嚴邊備，廣屯田，興學校，罪貪吏，徙頑民。

translations.literal: Within they cultivated government and teaching; without they tightened frontier defenses, expanded military colonies, established schools, punished corrupt officials, and relocated obstinate commoners.
translations.idiomatic: At home they strengthened governance and education; on the frontier they tightened defenses, expanded military colonies, established schools, punished corrupt officials, and relocated unruly commoners.

sentences.zh: 不數年間，朵兒只巴獻女，伯顏帖木兒、乃兒不花等相繼擒獲，納哈出亦降。

translations.literal: Within a few years Duojizhiba presented a daughter; Boyan Temur, Nir Buqa, and others were captured in succession, and Nahachu also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years Duojizhiba sent a daughter as tribute; Boyan Temur, Nir Buqa, and others were captured one after another, and Nahachu surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 此專務內治，不勤遠略之明效也。

translations.literal: This is the clear effect of devoting oneself to internal governance and not zealously pursuing far-reaching campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: This was the clear proof that focusing on internal governance rather than distant campaigns works.

sentences.zh: 伏望遠鑒漢、唐，近法太祖，毋以窮兵黷武為快，毋以犁庭掃穴為功。

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will take distant mirror from Han and Tang, take nearby model from Taizu, and not take exhausting the people through repeated warfare as pleasure, nor take uprooting the enemy's nest entirely as merit.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask Your Majesty to look to Han and Tang in the distant past and follow the Taizu Emperor's example in our own dynasty—do not relish exhausting the realm through ceaseless war, and do not treat the total destruction of distant enemies as the measure of achievement.

sentences.zh: 棄捐不毛之地，休養冠帶之民，俾竭力於田桑，盡心於庠序。

translations.literal: Abandon barren lands, restore and nurture the civilized people, and enable them to exert their strength in farming and sericulture and devote their hearts to schools.
translations.idiomatic: Abandon worthless frontier wasteland, give the people time to recover, and let them devote themselves to farming and to education.

sentences.zh: 邊塞絕傷痍之苦，閭里絕呻吟之聲。

translations.literal: The border fortresses would be free of the suffering of wounds, and the lanes and hamlets free of the sound of groaning.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier would know no war-wounded suffering, and villages would hear no cries of distress.

sentences.zh: 將無幸功，士無夭閼，遠人自服，荒外自歸。

translations.literal: Generals would not hope for unearned merit, scholars would not die young or have their paths blocked, distant peoples would submit of themselves, and the wild beyond would return of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Generals would not chase undeserved glory, scholars would not die young in vain, distant peoples would submit willingly, and the farthest wilds would come back into the fold.

sentences.zh: 國祚靈長於萬年矣。

translations.literal: The fortune of the state would be numinous and enduring for ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty's blessing would endure for ages.

sentences.zh: 其八曰官不在眾，在乎得人。

translations.literal: The eighth says: in governance the issue is not many officials, but obtaining the right men.
translations.idiomatic: The eighth: offices succeed not through their number, but through having the right people.

sentences.zh: 國家承大亂後，因時損益，以府為州，以州為縣。

translations.literal: The state, inheriting the aftermath of great disorder, adjusted according to the times—reducing fu to zhou and zhou to xian.
translations.idiomatic: After the great upheaval the state adjusted its administration to the times, demoting prefectures to sub-prefectures and sub-prefectures to counties.

sentences.zh: 繼又裁並小縣之糧不及俸者，量民數以設官。

translations.literal: Later it further merged small counties whose grain revenue did not cover official salaries, gauging the number of people to establish offices.
translations.idiomatic: Small counties whose tax revenue could not cover officials' salaries were merged, and posts were set according to population.

sentences.zh: 民多者縣設丞薄，少者知縣、典史而已。

translations.literal: Where the people were many the county was provided with an assistant magistrate and registrar; where few, only a magistrate and clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Populous counties had an assistant magistrate and registrar; smaller ones had only a magistrate and clerk.

sentences.zh: 其時官無廢事，民不愁勞。

translations.literal: At that time officials had no wasted tasks, and the people had no worry of toil.
translations.idiomatic: Then officials were not overburdened with idle posts, and the people were not overtaxed with labor.

sentences.zh: 今藩、臬二司及府、州、縣官，視洪武中再倍，政愈不理，民愈不寧，奸弊叢生，詐偽滋起。

translations.literal: Today provincial and surveillance commissions and prefectural, sub-prefectural, and county officials are twice as many as in the Hongwu era; governance grows more ungovernable, the people more unsettled, knavery proliferates, and fraud flourishes.
translations.idiomatic: Today provincial and surveillance commissions and local officials number twice what they did under Hongwu; government grows less effective, the people less secure, abuses multiply, and fraud spreads.

sentences.zh: 甚有官不能聽斷，吏不諳文移，乃容留書寫之人，在官影射，賄賂公行，獄訟淹滯，皆官冗吏濫所致也。

translations.literal: Some officials cannot even hear and decide cases, clerks do not understand official documents, yet they keep scribes on the premises who operate as hidden proxies; bribery is openly practiced and lawsuits drag on—all caused by redundant officials and excessive clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Some magistrates cannot even adjudicate cases, clerks do not understand official correspondence, yet they keep scribes on staff who act as hidden proxies; bribery runs rampant and lawsuits stall—all the result of too many officials and too many clerks.

sentences.zh: 望斷自宸衷，凡內外官吏，並依洪武中員額，冗濫者悉汰，則天工無曠，庶績咸熙，而天下大治矣。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will decide from his own heart that all inner and outer officials should follow the Hongwu quotas, and all redundant and excessive ones be eliminated; then no heavenly post will stand vacant, all achievements will flourish, and the empire will be greatly governed.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty decide in his own heart to restore all inner and outer offices to their Hongwu quotas and dismiss every redundant post; then every office will be filled by the worthy, every task well performed, and the empire truly well governed.

sentences.zh: 奏上，命廷臣議之。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted, and the emperor ordered the court ministers to deliberate on it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor ordered the court ministers to discuss it.

sentences.zh: 尚書呂震以為文辭冗長，且事多已行，不足采。

translations.literal: Minister Lü Zhen held that the language was verbose and lengthy, and that many matters had already been carried out, so it was not worth adopting.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Lü Zhen argued that the prose was too long and that many of its proposals had already been implemented, so it was not worth adopting.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「所言甚有學識，多契朕心，當察其素履以聞。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What was said shows great learning; much of it accords with my heart. His past conduct should be investigated and reported."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "These words show real learning, and much of it accords with my own thinking. Investigate his past conduct and report back."

sentences.zh: 震乃言：「濟故元進士，曾守郡，坐事戍邊。」

translations.literal: Zhen then said: "Ji was formerly a Yuan-dynasty jinshi; he once governed a commandery and was sent to the frontier in exile for an offense."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen then said: "Fan Ji was a jinshi under the Yuan; he once served as prefect and was exiled to the frontier for an offense."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「惜哉斯人！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What a pity, this man!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "What a pity—such a man!

sentences.zh: 令久淹行伍，今猶足用。」

translations.literal: He has long been kept in the ranks; even now he is still fit for use."
translations.idiomatic: He has languished in the ranks for years, yet he is still fit for service."

sentences.zh: 震曰：「年老矣。」

translations.literal: Zhen said: "He is old."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said: "He is too old."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「國家用人，正須老成，但不宜任以繁劇。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In employing men the state precisely needs seasoned experience, but he should not be given heavy and demanding duties."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The state needs seasoned men precisely because of their experience, but he should not be given heavy duties."

sentences.zh: 乃以濟為儒學訓導。

translations.literal: Ji was then appointed Confucian instructor.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ji was then appointed Confucian instructor.

sentences.zh: 聊讓，蘭州人。

translations.literal: Liao Rang was a man of Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liao Rang was a native of Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 肅府儀衛司余丁也。

translations.literal: He was a surplus soldier of the Su Prince's ceremonial guard command.
translations.idiomatic: He was a surplus soldier in the Su Prince's ceremonial guard command.

sentences.zh: 好學有誌尚，明習時務。

translations.literal: He loved learning and had lofty aims, and was well versed in current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and held high aspirations, and understood current affairs well.

sentences.zh: 景帝嗣位，懲王振蒙蔽，大辟言路，吏民皆得上書言事。

translations.literal: When the Jingdi Emperor succeeded to the throne, chastising Wang Zhen's deception of the court, he greatly opened the path of remonstrance, and officials and commoners alike could submit memorials on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingdi Emperor succeeded to the throne, determined to correct Wang Zhen's deception of the court, he widely opened the path of remonstrance, and officials and commoners alike could submit memorials on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年六月，讓詣闕陳數事，其略曰：

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of the Jingtai reign, Rang came to court and submitted several matters; the gist was as follows:
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the first year of Jingtai, Rang came to court and submitted several proposals; in summary he said:

sentences.zh: 邇歲土木繁興，異端盛起，番僧絡驛，汙吏縱橫，相臣不正其非，御史不劾其罪，上下蒙蔽，民生雕瘵。

translations.literal: In recent years construction projects have flourished, heterodox teachings have risen in strength, Tibetan monks fill the relay stations, corrupt officials run rampant, chief ministers do not correct their wrongs, censors do not impeach their crimes, upper and lower levels conceal one another, and the people's livelihood is wasted and afflicted.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years construction has flourished, heterodox teachings spread, Tibetan monks crowd the relay stations, corrupt officials run unchecked, chief ministers fail to correct abuses, censors fail to impeach wrongdoers, the court and the provinces conceal one another, and the people's livelihood is ruined.

sentences.zh: 狡寇犯邊，上皇播越。

translations.literal: Crafty bandits violated the frontier, and the former emperor was cast into exile.
translations.idiomatic: Crafty enemies invaded the frontier, and the former emperor was driven into exile.

sentences.zh: 陛下枕戈嘗膽之秋，可不拔賢舉能，一新政治乎？

translations.literal: At this season when Your Majesty sleeps on spears and tastes gall, can you not raise the worthy and promote the capable to renew governance entirely?
translations.idiomatic: At this moment when Your Majesty sleeps on spears and tastes gall in resolve, should you not raise the worthy, promote the capable, and renew the whole conduct of government?

sentences.zh: 昔宗、嶽為將，敵國不敢呼名；

translations.literal: Formerly when Zong and Yue served as generals, enemy states did not dare speak their names;
translations.idiomatic: When Zong Ze and Yue Fei commanded armies, enemy states did not dare speak their names aloud;

sentences.zh: 韓、範鎮邊，西賊聞之破膽。

translations.literal: when Han and Fan guarded the frontier, western bandits heard of them and their gall split.
translations.idiomatic: when Han Qi and Fan Zhongyan guarded the frontier, western raiders lost heart at the mere mention of them.

sentences.zh: 司馬光居相位，強鄰戒勿犯邊。

translations.literal: When Sima Guang held the chancellorship, powerful neighbors were warned not to violate the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Guang served as chief minister, powerful neighbors were warned not to violate the border.

sentences.zh: 今文武大臣之有威名德望者，宜使典樞要，且延訪智術才能之士，布滿朝廷，則也先必畏服，而上皇可指日還矣。

translations.literal: Today civil and military ministers who possess renown and moral standing should be made to hold key posts, and men of wisdom, skill, and talent should be sought out and spread throughout the court; then Esen will surely fear and submit, and the former emperor can return within days.
translations.idiomatic: Today civil and military ministers of proven reputation and standing should hold the key posts, and men of wisdom and talent should be sought out and placed throughout the court; then Esen would surely be overawed, and the former emperor could return within days.

sentences.zh: 大臣，陽也；

translations.literal: Ministers are yang;
translations.idiomatic: Ministers are yang;

sentences.zh: 宦寺，陰也。

translations.literal: eunuchs are yin.
translations.idiomatic: eunuchs are yin.

sentences.zh: 君子，陽也；

translations.literal: The noble man is yang;
translations.idiomatic: Noble men are yang;

sentences.zh: 小人，陰也。

translations.literal: the petty man is yin.
translations.idiomatic: petty men are yin.

sentences.zh: 近日食地震，陰盛陽微，謫見天地。

translations.literal: Recently there have been eclipses and earthquakes; yin is strong and yang weak—a reproach revealed by Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Recently there have been eclipses and earthquakes—yin has grown strong and yang has weakened, a reproach sent from Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 望陛下總攬乾綱，抑宦寺使不得預政，遏小人俾不得居位，則陰陽順而天變弭矣。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will gather up the imperial authority, restrain eunuchs so they may not participate in government, and check petty men so they may not hold office; then yin and yang will be in order and heavenly anomalies will cease.
translations.idiomatic: I ask Your Majesty to hold the reins of power firmly, keep eunuchs from meddling in government, and block petty men from office; then yin and yang will be balanced and Heaven's warnings will cease.

sentences.zh: 天下治亂，在君心邪正。

translations.literal: Whether the empire is governed or in disorder depends on whether the ruler's heart is crooked or straight.
translations.idiomatic: Whether the empire is well governed or in chaos depends on whether the ruler's heart is upright.

sentences.zh: 田獵是娛，宮室是侈，宦寺是狎，三者有一，足蠱君心。

translations.literal: Taking field hunting as pleasure, taking palace building as extravagance, taking intimacy with eunuchs as familiarity—if any one of these three exists, it is enough to bewitch the ruler's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Field hunting for pleasure, palace building for display, and intimacy with eunuchs—any one of these three is enough to corrupt the ruler's heart.

sentences.zh: 願陛下涵養克治，多接賢士大夫，少親宦官宮妾，自能革奢靡，戒遊佚，而心無不正矣。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would cultivate and restrain himself, receive worthy scholar-officials often, and keep close company with eunuchs and palace women less; then he will naturally reform extravagance, guard against idleness, and his heart will be without crookedness.
translations.idiomatic: I ask Your Majesty to cultivate self-restraint, spend more time with worthy scholar-officials, and keep less company with eunuchs and palace women; then extravagance will be curbed, idleness checked, and the heart kept upright.

sentences.zh: 堯立謗木，恐人不言，所以聖；

translations.literal: Yao erected a criticism board, fearing that people would not speak—therefore he was sage;
translations.idiomatic: Yao erected a criticism board because he feared people would not speak out—that is why he was sage;

sentences.zh: 秦除謚法，恐人議己，所以亡。

translations.literal: Qin abolished the posthumous-title law, fearing that people would criticize him—therefore it perished.
translations.idiomatic: Qin abolished the law of posthumous titles because he feared people would criticize him—that is why it fell.

sentences.zh: 陛下廣從諫之量，旌直言之臣，則國家利弊，閭閻休戚，臣下無所顧忌，而言無不盡矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty broadens the measure for accepting remonstrance and honors ministers who speak directly, then the benefits and harms of the state and the joys and sorrows of the lanes and wards—subordinates will have nothing to fear, and nothing will go unsaid.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty broadens his capacity to accept remonstrance and honors those who speak plainly, then on matters of national benefit and harm and the welfare of the people, officials will speak without fear and nothing will be left unsaid.

sentences.zh: 蘇子曰：「平居無犯顏敢諫之臣，則臨難必無仗節死義之士。」

translations.literal: Master Su said: "In ordinary times there are no ministers who risk offense and dare remonstrate; then in crisis there will surely be no men who uphold integrity and die for righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi said: "If in ordinary times there are no ministers who risk offense to speak plainly, then in crisis there will surely be no men who uphold their integrity and die for principle."

sentences.zh: 願陛下恒念是言而審察之。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would constantly keep these words in mind and examine them carefully.
translations.idiomatic: I ask Your Majesty to keep these words always in mind and weigh them carefully.

sentences.zh: 書奏，帝頗嘉納之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor greatly approved and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor largely approved it.

sentences.zh: 後四年，讓登進士。

translations.literal: Four years later Rang passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later Liao Rang passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 官知縣卒。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate and died in office.

sentences.zh: 景泰二年，監生郭佑亦上書言兵事，略曰：

translations.literal: In the second year of the Jingtai reign, the student Guo You also submitted a memorial on military affairs, saying in summary:
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Jingtai reign, the Imperial Academy student Guo You also submitted a memorial on military affairs, saying in summary:

sentences.zh: 逆寇犯順，上皇蒙塵，此千古非常之變，百世必報之仇也。

translations.literal: Rebellious bandits violated righteousness, and the former emperor suffered disgrace in the dust—this is an extraordinary change for a thousand ages and a feud that must be repaid for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellious enemies violated the realm, and the former emperor suffered disgrace—this is an upheaval without parallel in a thousand years and a wrong that must be avenged for generations.

sentences.zh: 今使臣之來，動以數千，務驕蹇責望於我，而我乃隱忍姑息，致賊勢日張，我氣日索，求和與和，求戰與戰，是和戰之權，不在我而在賊也。

translations.literal: Now when their envoys come, they arrive by the thousands, insisting on arrogance and pressing demands upon us, while we forbear and indulge them, causing the bandits' strength to grow daily and our spirit to shrink daily; we seek peace and they grant peace, we seek war and they grant war—the power over peace and war lies not with us but with the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Now their envoys arrive by the thousands, arrogant and demanding, while we forbear and indulge them; the enemy grows stronger by the day and our resolve weaker. We ask for peace and they decide whether to grant it; we ask for war and they decide whether to fight—the choice between peace and war is no longer ours but theirs.

sentences.zh: 願陛下結人心，親賢良，以固國本，廣儲蓄，練將士，以壯國氣。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would bind the hearts of the people, draw close to the worthy and good to solidify the foundation of the state, broaden reserves, and drill generals and soldiers to strengthen the nation's spirit.
translations.idiomatic: I ask Your Majesty to win the people's hearts, draw close to the worthy and good to strengthen the foundations of the state, build up reserves, and train generals and soldiers to restore national confidence.

sentences.zh: 正分定名，裁之以義。

translations.literal: Set right distinctions and fix names, and cut them off with righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Restore proper distinctions and fixed names, and restrain the enemy with righteousness.

sentences.zh: 如桀驁侵軼，則提兵問罪。

translations.literal: If they are arrogant and encroach and violate, then raise troops to demand punishment.
translations.idiomatic: If they grow arrogant and encroach, then march against them and demand justice.

sentences.zh: 使大漠之南，不敢有匹馬闌入，乃可保百年無虞。

translations.literal: Make it so that south of the Great Desert not a single horse dares cross the border; only then can a century pass without worry.
translations.idiomatic: Ensure that south of the desert not a single horse dare cross the border—only then can peace be kept for a hundred years.

sentences.zh: 不然西北力罷，東南財竭，不能一日安枕矣。

translations.literal: Otherwise the northwest will be exhausted in strength and the southeast drained of wealth, and one cannot rest easy for a single day.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the northwest will be exhausted and the southeast drained of wealth, and not even one night's sleep will be secure.

sentences.zh: 昨以國用耗乏，謀國大臣欲紓一時之急，令民納粟者賜冠帶。

translations.literal: Recently, because state revenue was depleted, ministers planning for the state wished to relieve the urgency of the moment and ordered that those who contributed grain be granted cap-and-belt honors.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, because state revenue was depleted, ministers seeking to relieve the immediate crisis ordered that those who contributed grain be granted cap-and-belt honors.

sentences.zh: 今軍旅稍寧，行之如故。

translations.literal: Now that the army is somewhat settled, the practice continues as before.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the army is somewhat settled, the practice continues unchanged.

sentences.zh: 農工商販之徒，不較賢愚，惟財是授。

translations.literal: Among farmers, craftsmen, merchants, and peddlers, worthiness and foolishness are not weighed—only wealth is rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers, craftsmen, merchants, and peddlers receive honors without regard to merit—wealth alone decides.

sentences.zh: 驕親戚，誇鄉里，長非分之邪心。

translations.literal: They make their kin proud, boast to their home districts, and nurture improper and crooked hearts.
translations.idiomatic: They flaunt their standing before kin and neighbors and nurture improper ambition.

sentences.zh: 贓汙吏罷退為民，欲掩閭黨之恥，納粟納草，冠帶而歸。

translations.literal: Corrupt officials dismissed and returned to the people, wishing to cover the shame before their lanes and clans, contribute grain and fodder, and return wearing cap and belt.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt officials dismissed from office, seeking to hide their shame before neighbors and clans, buy their way back with grain and fodder and return wearing cap and belt.

sentences.zh: 前以冒貨去職，今以輸貨得官，何以禁貪殘、重名爵？

translations.literal: Formerly they lost office for seeking goods improperly; now they gain office for delivering goods—how can greed and cruelty be forbidden and noble titles be held in esteem?
translations.idiomatic: Once they lost office for taking bribes; now they regain rank by paying for it—how can greed be checked or noble titles be held in esteem?

sentences.zh: 況天下統一，藏富在民，未至大不得已，而舉措如此，是以空乏啟寇心也。

translations.literal: Moreover the empire is unified and wealth is stored among the people; we have not yet reached a point of great necessity, yet measures such as these are taken—thus emptiness and want open the bandits' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the empire is unified and wealth lies with the people; we have not yet reached true necessity, yet we take measures like these—showing weakness and inviting enemy ambition.

sentences.zh: 章下廷議，格不行。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down for court deliberation and was blocked from implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the court for deliberation and was rejected.

sentences.zh: 又有胡仲倫者，雲南鹽課提舉司吏目也。

translations.literal: There was also Hu Zhonglun, a petty clerk in the Yunnan Salt Tax Intendant Office.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Hu Zhonglun, a petty clerk in the Yunnan Salt Tax Intendant Office.

sentences.zh: 緣事入都，會上皇北狩，也先欲妻以妹，上皇因遣廣寧伯劉安入言於帝。

translations.literal: On business he entered the capital; it happened that the former emperor was on the northern hunt, Esen wished to marry him to his younger sister, and the former emperor therefore sent the Marquis Liu An of Guangning to enter and speak to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He came to the capital on business just as the former emperor was taken north; Esen wished to marry him to his sister, and the former emperor sent the Marquis Liu An of Guangning to relay the proposal to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 仲倫上疏爭之，言：「今日事不可屈者有七。

translations.literal: Zhonglun submitted a memorial disputing it, saying: "In today's affairs there are seven matters on which we cannot yield.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonglun submitted a memorial objecting, saying: "In the present crisis there are seven points on which we must not yield.

sentences.zh: 降萬乘之尊，與諧婚媾，一也。

translations.literal: To lower the dignity of the Son of Heaven and enter into marriage alliance—this is the first.
translations.idiomatic: To lower the dignity of the sovereign and enter into marriage alliance—this is the first.

sentences.zh: 敵假和議，使我無備，二也。

translations.literal: The enemy feigns peace talks to leave us unprepared—this is the second.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy feigns peace talks to catch us unprepared—this is the second.

sentences.zh: 必欲為姻，驕尊自大，三也。

translations.literal: If they insist on marriage, they grow arrogant and self-important—this is the third.
translations.idiomatic: If they insist on marriage, they will grow arrogant and overbearing—this is the third.

sentences.zh: 索金帛，使我坐困，四也。

translations.literal: Demanding gold and silk leaves us sitting in distress—this is the fourth.
translations.idiomatic: Demanding gold and silk will leave us financially exhausted—this is the fourth.

sentences.zh: 以送駕為名，乘機入犯，五也。

translations.literal: Under the pretext of escorting the imperial carriage, they seize the opportunity to invade—this is the fifth.
translations.idiomatic: Under the pretext of escorting the emperor home, they will seize the chance to invade—this is the fifth.

sentences.zh: 逼上皇手詔，誘取邊城，六也。

translations.literal: Coercing an edict in the former emperor's own hand to lure away frontier cities—this is the sixth.
translations.idiomatic: Coercing an edict in the former emperor's own hand to extract frontier cities—this is the sixth.

sentences.zh: 欲求山後之地，七也。

translations.literal: Seeking the lands behind the mountains—this is the seventh.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking the lands behind the mountains—this is the seventh.

sentences.zh: 稍從其一，大事去矣。

translations.literal: Yield even slightly on any one of these, and the great cause is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Yield on even one of these, and the great cause is lost.

sentences.zh: 曩上皇在位，王振專權。

translations.literal: Formerly when the former emperor was on the throne, Wang Zhen monopolized power.
translations.idiomatic: When the former emperor was on the throne, Wang Zhen monopolized power.

sentences.zh: 忠諫者死，鯁直者戍；

translations.literal: Those who loyally remonstrated died; those who were blunt and upright were sent to the frontier;
translations.idiomatic: Those who loyally remonstrated were put to death; those who spoke bluntly were exiled;

sentences.zh: 君子見斥，小人驟遷。

translations.literal: noble men were expelled, petty men were suddenly promoted.
translations.idiomatic: noble men were driven out and petty men promoted overnight.

sentences.zh: 章奏多決中旨，黑白混淆，邪正倒置。

translations.literal: Memorials were mostly decided by secret imperial will; black and white were confused and crooked and straight inverted.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials were mostly decided by secret imperial edict; right and wrong were confused and the wicked and the upright reversed.

sentences.zh: 閩、浙之寇方殷，瓦剌之釁大作。

translations.literal: Bandits in Min and Zhe were just then raging, and the Oirat provocation broke out on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry in Fujian and Zhejiang was raging, and the Oirat launched a major attack.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜親賢遠奸，信賞必罰，通上情，達下誌。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should draw close to the worthy and keep distant from the wicked, keep faith in rewards and certainty in punishments, communicate the sentiments above, and reach the will below.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should draw close to the worthy and keep the wicked at a distance, reward faithfully and punish surely, understand conditions at court, and heed the will of the people.

sentences.zh: 賣國之奸無所投隙，倉卒之變末由發機，朝廷自此尊，天下自此安矣。」

translations.literal: Traitors who would sell the state would have nowhere to insert themselves, sudden crises would have no opening from which to arise, the court from this would be honored, and the empire from this would be secure."
translations.idiomatic: Traitors who would sell out the state would find no opening, sudden crises would have no chance to erupt, the court would regain its dignity, and the empire would be secure."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納焉。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 又有華敏者，南京錦衣軍余也。

translations.literal: There was also Hua Min, a surplus soldier of the Nanjing Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Hua Min, a surplus soldier of the Nanjing Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 意氣慷慨，讀書通大義，憤王振亂國，與儕輩言輒裂眥怒詈。

translations.literal: Bold and generous in spirit, he read books and grasped great principle; indignant that Wang Zhen had thrown the state into disorder, whenever he spoke with his companions he would split his eyes in rage and curse.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and high-spirited, he read widely and grasped great principle; furious that Wang Zhen had thrown the state into chaos, he would speak with blazing eyes and bitter curses among his comrades.

sentences.zh: 景泰三年九月上書曰：

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year of the Jingtai reign he submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the third year of the Jingtai reign he submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 近年以來，內官袁琦、唐受、喜寧、王振專權害政，致國事傾危。

translations.literal: In recent years the inner officials Yuan Qi, Tang Shou, Xi Ning, and Wang Zhen have monopolized power and harmed government, causing state affairs to lean toward crisis.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the eunuchs Yuan Qi, Tang Shou, Xi Ning, and Wang Zhen monopolized power and harmed government, bringing the state to the brink of collapse.

sentences.zh: 望陛下防微杜漸，總攬權綱，為子孫萬世法。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will guard against the subtle and stop the gradual, gather up the reins of power, and make this a model for descendants for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: I ask Your Majesty to check abuses at the first sign, hold the reins of power firmly, and set an example for generations to come.

sentences.zh: 不然恐禍稔蕭墻，曹節、侯覽之害，復見於今日。

translations.literal: Otherwise I fear disaster will ripen within the palace walls, and the harm of Cao Jie and Hou Lan will appear again in our own day.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise disaster will ripen within the palace walls, and the evils of Cao Jie and Hou Lan will appear again in our own day.

sentences.zh: 臣雖賤陋，不勝痛哭流涕。

translations.literal: Your servant, though base and lowly, cannot bear it and weeps bitterly with streaming tears.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant, though lowly and obscure, cannot contain his grief and weeps bitterly.

sentences.zh: 謹以虐軍害民十事，為陛下痛切言之。

translations.literal: Respectfully, on ten matters of abusing the army and harming the people, I speak to Your Majesty with painful urgency.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully set forth ten ways in which the army is abused and the people harmed, and speak to Your Majesty with urgent grief.

sentences.zh: 內官家積金銀珠玉，累室兼籯，從何而至？

translations.literal: In eunuchs' households gold, silver, pearls, and jade are piled—rooms overflowing and baskets heaped full; whence do these come?
translations.idiomatic: In eunuchs' households gold, silver, pearls, and jade fill room after room—where does it all come from?

sentences.zh: 非內盜府藏，則外朘民膏。

translations.literal: If not by stealing from the inner treasury, then by draining the people's fat without.
translations.idiomatic: Either they steal from the imperial treasury, or they bleed the people dry.

sentences.zh: 害一也。

translations.literal: This is the first harm.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first harm.

sentences.zh: 怙勢矜寵，占公侯邸舍，興作工役，勞擾軍民。

translations.literal: Relying on power and presuming on favor, they occupy the mansions of dukes and marquises, launch construction projects, and toil and disturb soldiers and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on power and imperial favor, they seize the mansions of dukes and marquises, launch construction projects, and burden soldiers and civilians with forced labor.

sentences.zh: 害二也。

translations.literal: This is the second harm.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second harm.

sentences.zh: 家人外親，皆市井無籍之子，縱橫豪悍，任意作奸，納粟補官，貴賤淆雜。

translations.literal: Their household members and outside kin are all sons of the marketplace without registration; they roam freely, fierce and overbearing, commit wrongdoing at will, buy office by contributing grain, and noble and base are confused together.
translations.idiomatic: Their household members and outside kin are all unregistered riffraff from the marketplace; they roam freely, violent and overbearing, commit crimes at will, buy office by contributing grain, and blur the line between noble and base.

sentences.zh: 害三也。

translations.literal: This is the third harm.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third harm.

sentences.zh: 建造佛寺，耗費不貲，營一己之私，破萬家之產。

translations.literal: Building Buddhist temples, the expenditure is incalculable; serving one man's private interest, they ruin ten thousand households' property.
translations.idiomatic: They build Buddhist temples at incalculable cost, pursuing private gain while ruining the livelihood of countless families.

sentences.zh: 害四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth harm.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth harm.

sentences.zh: 廣置田莊，不入賦稅，寄戶郡縣，不受征徭，阡陌連亙，而民無立錐。

translations.literal: They widely establish estate fields, not entering tax registers; register households in commanderies and counties, not receiving levies and corvée; field paths connect continuously, yet the people have no space to stand an awl.
translations.idiomatic: They amass vast estates, evade tax registers, lodge their households in counties to escape levies and corvée, and stretch their fields from horizon to horizon until the people have not a pin's point of land to call their own.

sentences.zh: 害五也。

translations.literal: This is the fifth harm.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth harm.

sentences.zh: 家人中鹽，虛占引數，轉而售人，倍支鉅萬，壞國家法，豪奪商利。

translations.literal: Household members obtain salt licenses, falsely occupy quota numbers, turn and sell to others, profiting tens of thousands in multiples, ruining the state's laws, forcibly seizing merchants' profits.
translations.idiomatic: Their household members obtain salt licenses, hoard quota certificates, resell them at a markup for tens of thousands in profit, violate the salt laws, and seize merchants' profits by force.

sentences.zh: 害六也。

translations.literal: This is the sixth harm.
translations.idiomatic: This is the sixth harm.

sentences.zh: 奏求塌房，邀接商旅，倚勢賒買，恃強不償，行賈坐敝，莫敢誰何。

translations.literal: They memorialize requesting warehouse sheds, invite and receive traveling merchants, rely on power to buy on credit, depend on force and not repay, itinerant merchants sit ruined, none dare ask who or why.
translations.idiomatic: They petition for warehouse sheds, lure traveling merchants, buy on credit by force of position, refuse to pay what they owe, and ruin itinerant traders until none dare protest.

sentences.zh: 害七也。

translations.literal: This is the seventh harm.
translations.idiomatic: This is the seventh harm.

sentences.zh: 賣放軍匠，名為伴當，俾辦月錢，致內府監局營作乏人，工役煩重，並力不足。

translations.literal: They sell and release military artisans, named substitute attendants, made to supply monthly payments, causing the inner palace supervisory offices' construction to lack men, labor service burdensome and heavy, combined strength insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: They sell off military artisans as "substitute attendants" who must pay monthly fees, leaving the palace workshops short-handed so that burdensome projects exceed available labor.

sentences.zh: 害八也。

translations.literal: This is the eighth harm.
translations.idiomatic: This is the eighth harm.

sentences.zh: 家人貿置物料，所司畏懼，以一科十，虧官損民。

translations.literal: Household members trade and procure materials; the responsible offices fear and dread; for one unit they levy ten, harming the government and injuring the people.
translations.idiomatic: When their household members trade in supplies, the responsible offices tremble before them, charging tenfold for what should cost one—shortchanging the state and harming the people.

sentences.zh: 害九也。

translations.literal: This is the ninth harm.
translations.idiomatic: This is the ninth harm.

sentences.zh: 監作所至，非法酷刑，軍匠塗炭，不勝怨酷。

translations.literal: Where supervision of construction arrives, illegal harsh punishments; military artisans wallow in charcoal, unable to bear resentment and cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever they supervise construction, they inflict illegal tortures; military artisans suffer agony beyond what bitter hatred can express.

sentences.zh: 害十也。

translations.literal: This is the tenth harm.
translations.idiomatic: This is the tenth harm.

sentences.zh: 章下禮部，寢不行。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the Ministry of Rites, and it lay dormant without implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the Ministry of Rites, but nothing was done.

sentences.zh: 又有賈斌者，商河人，山西都司令史也。

translations.literal: There was also Jia Bin, a man of Shanghe, a clerk of the Shanxi Regional Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Jia Bin, a native of Shanghe and a clerk of the Shanxi Regional Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 亦疏言宦官之害，引漢桓帝、唐文宗、宋徽欽為戒。

translations.literal: He too submitted a memorial on the harm of eunuchs, citing Emperor Huan of Han, Emperor Wenzong of Tang, and the Hui and Qin emperors of Song as warnings.
translations.idiomatic: He too submitted a memorial on the harm of eunuchs, citing Emperor Huan of Han, Emperor Wenzong of Tang, and the emperors Hui and Qin of Song as warnings.

sentences.zh: 且獻所輯《忠義集》四卷，采史傳所記直諫盡忠守節之士，而宦官恃寵蠹政，可為鑒戒者附焉，乞命工刊布。

translations.literal: Moreover he presented the four scrolls of his compiled Collection of Loyal Righteousness, gathering from histories and biographies those who remonstrated directly, exhausted loyalty, and preserved integrity, while attaching examples of eunuchs relying on favor to ruin government that may serve as warnings, and begged that craftsmen be ordered to print and circulate it.
translations.idiomatic: He also presented four scrolls of his compiled Collection of Loyal Righteousness, drawing from historical records examples of men who spoke bluntly, gave their all in loyalty, and held to their integrity, with appended cases of eunuchs who abused imperial favor to ruin government as warnings, and asked that it be printed and circulated.

sentences.zh: 禮部以其言當，乞垂鑒納，不必刊行。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites judged his words correct and asked that the emperor reflect and accept them, without need to print and circulate.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites judged his words sound and asked the emperor to reflect on and accept them, without need to print and circulate the book.

sentences.zh: 帝報聞。

translations.literal: The emperor acknowledged receipt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor acknowledged receipt.

sentences.zh: 左鼎，字周器，永新人。

translations.literal: Zuo Ding, courtesy name Zhouqi, was a man of Yongxin.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Ding, courtesy name Zhouqi, was a native of Yongxin.

sentences.zh: 正統七年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the seventh year of the Zhengtong reign.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the seventh year of the Zhengtong reign.

sentences.zh: 明年，都御史王文以御史多闕，請會吏部於進士選補。

translations.literal: The next year, Censor-in-Chief Wang Wen, because many censor posts were vacant, requested to meet with the Ministry of Personnel to select and fill from jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, because many censor posts stood vacant, Censor-in-Chief Wang Wen asked to meet with the Ministry of Personnel and fill them from among the jinshi.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 尚書王直考鼎及白圭等十餘人，曉諳刑名，皆授御史。

translations.literal: Minister Wang Zhi examined Ding and Bai Gui and more than ten others, versed in penal codes, all appointed censors.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wang Zhi examined Ding, Bai Gui, and more than ten others who were versed in penal law, and all were appointed censors.

sentences.zh: 而鼎得南京。

translations.literal: And Ding was assigned to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Ding was assigned to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 尋改北，巡按山西。

translations.literal: Soon transferred north, inspecting Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred north and sent to inspect Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 時英宗北狩，兵荒洊臻。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Yingzong was captive in the north, warfare and famine repeatedly arrived.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Emperor Yingzong was held captive in the north, and warfare and famine struck in succession.

sentences.zh: 請蠲太原諸府稅糧，停大同轉餉夫，以蘇其困。

translations.literal: He requested remission of tax grain in Taiyuan and other prefectures, halting Datong transport corvée, to relieve their distress.
translations.idiomatic: He requested remission of tax grain in Taiyuan and other prefectures and a halt to Datong transport corvée to relieve their distress.

sentences.zh: 也先請和，抗言不可。

translations.literal: Esen requested peace; he spoke out against it, saying it should not be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen requested peace, he spoke out against it, declaring it must not be accepted.

sentences.zh: 尋以山東、河南饑，遣鼎巡視，民賴以安。

translations.literal: Soon because Shandong and Henan suffered famine, Ding was sent to inspect; the people relied on this and were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, because Shandong and Henan were stricken with famine, Ding was sent to inspect the region, and the people were thereby relieved.

sentences.zh: 律，官吏故勘平人致死者抵罪，時以給事中於泰言，悉得寬貰。

translations.literal: The law: officials who through deliberate investigation cause commoners' death pay with their lives; at the time, on Supervising Secretary Yu Tai's recommendation, all received leniency.
translations.idiomatic: The law held that officials who through deliberate investigation caused the death of commoners should pay with their lives; but at the time, on Supervising Secretary Yu Tai's recommendation, all such cases received leniency.

sentences.zh: 鼎言：「小民無知，情貸可也。

translations.literal: Ding said: "Commoners are ignorant; lenient treatment is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Ding said: "Commoners are ignorant; leniency is acceptable.

sentences.zh: 官吏深文巧詆，與故殺何異？

translations.literal: Officials who twist the law with crafty accusations—how is this different from deliberate killing?
translations.idiomatic: But officials who twist the law with crafty accusations—how is that different from deliberate killing?

sentences.zh: 法者，天下之公，不可意為輕重。」

translations.literal: The law is the public standard of the realm; its severity cannot be decided by whim."
translations.idiomatic: The law is the public standard of the realm; its severity cannot be decided at whim."

sentences.zh: 自是論如律。

translations.literal: From then on, judgments followed the law.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, judgments followed the law.

sentences.zh: 景泰四年疏言：

translations.literal: In the fourth year of the Jingtai reign he submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Jingtai reign he submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 瓦剌變作，將士無用，由軍政不立。

translations.literal: When the Oirat crisis erupted, officers and soldiers were useless, because military administration was not established.
translations.idiomatic: When the Oirat crisis erupted, officers and soldiers proved useless because military administration had not been established.

sentences.zh: 謂必痛懲前弊，乃今又五年矣。

translations.literal: It was said the previous abuses must be sternly punished, yet now another five years have passed.
translations.idiomatic: It was said the previous abuses must be sternly punished, yet five more years have passed.

sentences.zh: 貂蟬盈座，悉屬公侯；

translations.literal: Ranked caps fill the seats, all belonging to dukes and marquises;
translations.idiomatic: Ranked caps fill the seats, all belonging to dukes and marquises;

sentences.zh: 鞍馬塞途，莫非將帥。

translations.literal: Saddles and horses choke the roads, none not generals and commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Saddles and horses choke the roads, and every rider is a general or commander.

sentences.zh: 民財歲耗，國帑日虛。

translations.literal: The people's wealth is exhausted year by year, the state treasury grows empty day by day.
translations.idiomatic: The people's wealth is drained year by year, and the state treasury grows emptier by the day.

sentences.zh: 以天下之大，土地兵甲之眾，曾不能振揚威武，則軍政仍未立也。

translations.literal: With so vast an empire and so many lands, troops, and arms, yet unable to display martial prestige, then military administration is still not established.
translations.idiomatic: With so vast an empire and so many lands, troops, and arms, the state still cannot display martial prestige—military administration remains unestablished.

sentences.zh: 昔太祖定律令，至太宗，暫許有罪者贖，蓋權宜也。

translations.literal: Formerly the Founding Emperor fixed laws and ordinances; by the time of the Taizong Emperor, temporary permission was granted for the guilty to redeem punishment—this was expedient policy.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Founding Emperor fixed laws and ordinances; under the Taizong Emperor, temporary permission was granted for the guilty to redeem punishment—an expedient measure.

sentences.zh: 乃法吏拘牽，沿為成例，官吏受枉法財，悉得減贖。

translations.literal: Yet legal clerks clung rigidly and made it a standing precedent; officials who received bribes under perverted law all could have punishment reduced by redemption.
translations.idiomatic: Yet legal clerks clung rigidly to this and made it a standing precedent, so officials who took bribes under perverted law could all have their punishments reduced by redemption.

sentences.zh: 骫骳如此，復何顧憚哉。

translations.literal: Corruption such as this—what further fear or restraint is there?
translations.idiomatic: With corruption so deep, what further fear or restraint can there be?

sentences.zh: 國初建官有常，近始因事增設。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state, offices were established with fixed numbers; only recently have posts been added according to events.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the state, offices were established in fixed numbers; only recently have posts been added as events arose.

sentences.zh: 主事每司二人，今有增至十人者矣。

translations.literal: Section chiefs were two per department; now some departments have increased to ten.
translations.idiomatic: Section chiefs were two per department; now some departments have as many as ten.

sentences.zh: 御史六十人，今則百餘人矣。

translations.literal: Censors were sixty; now there are more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Censors numbered sixty; now there are more than a hundred.

sentences.zh: 甚至一部有兩尚書，侍郎亦倍常額，都御史以數十計，此京官之冗也。

translations.literal: Some ministries even have two ministers; vice ministers also double the usual quota; censor-in-chiefs number in the dozens—this is the redundancy of capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: Some ministries even have two ministers; vice ministers also exceed the usual quota; censor-in-chiefs number in the dozens—this is the redundancy of capital officials.

sentences.zh: 外則增設撫民、管屯官。

translations.literal: Outside, pacification and garrison-farming officials were added.
translations.idiomatic: In the provinces, pacification and garrison-farming officials were added.

sentences.zh: 如河南參議，益二而為四，僉事益三而為七，此外官之冗也。

translations.literal: For example, Henan's administrative commissioners increased by two to become four, and assistant commissioners increased by three to become seven—this is the redundancy of outside officials.
translations.idiomatic: In Henan, for example, administrative commissioners increased from two to four, and assistant commissioners from three to seven—this is the redundancy of provincial officials.

sentences.zh: 天下布、按二司各十餘人，乃歲遣御史巡視，復遣大臣巡撫鎮守。

translations.literal: Throughout the empire, each provincial administration and surveillance commission has more than ten officials, yet each year censors are dispatched to inspect, and grand ministers are again dispatched as grand coordinators and military pacifiers.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the empire, each provincial administration and surveillance commission already has more than ten officials, yet each year censors are dispatched to inspect, and grand ministers are again sent as grand coordinators and military pacifiers.

sentences.zh: 夫今之巡撫鎮守，即曩之方面御史也。

translations.literal: Now the grand coordinators and military pacifiers are exactly the former regional censors.
translations.idiomatic: Today's grand coordinators and military pacifiers are exactly the former regional censors.

sentences.zh: 為方面御史，則合眾人之長而不足；

translations.literal: As regional censors, combining the strengths of many was not enough;
translations.idiomatic: As regional censors, combining the strengths of many was not enough;

sentences.zh: 為巡撫鎮守，則任一人之智而有餘。

translations.literal: As grand coordinators and military pacifiers, relying on one man's wisdom is more than enough.
translations.idiomatic: As grand coordinators and military pacifiers, relying on one man's wisdom is more than enough.

sentences.zh: 有是理邪？

translations.literal: Is there such a principle?
translations.idiomatic: Is there such a principle?

sentences.zh: 至御史遷轉太驟，當以六年為率。

translations.literal: As for censors, transfer is too sudden; six years should be the standard.
translations.idiomatic: As for censors, transfers come too quickly; six years should be the standard.

sentences.zh: 令其通達政事，然後可以治人。

translations.literal: Let them thoroughly understand government affairs, and only then may they govern others.
translations.idiomatic: They should thoroughly understand government affairs before they are fit to govern others.

sentences.zh: 巡按所系尤重，毋使初任之員，漫然嘗試。

translations.literal: Touring inspection bears especially heavy responsibility; do not let newly appointed men casually experiment.
translations.idiomatic: Touring inspection bears especially heavy responsibility; newly appointed men must not be allowed to experiment casually.

sentences.zh: 其餘百執事，皆當慎擇而久任之。

translations.literal: All other functionaries should likewise be carefully chosen and long retained.
translations.idiomatic: All other functionaries should likewise be carefully chosen and retained for longer terms.

sentences.zh: 帝頗嘉納。

translations.literal: The emperor quite praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor largely approved and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復言：國家承平數十年，公私之積未充。

translations.literal: Before long he spoke again: the state had enjoyed peace for decades, yet public and private stores were not full.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he spoke again: the state had enjoyed peace for decades, yet public and private stores were still not full.

sentences.zh: 一遇軍興，抑配橫征，鬻官市爵，率行衰世茍且之政，此司邦計者過也。

translations.literal: Once military campaigns arise, forced apportionment and arbitrary levies, selling office and trading titles, generally practicing the makeshift policies of a declining age—this is the fault of those who manage state finance.
translations.idiomatic: Once war breaks out, forced apportionment and arbitrary levies, selling office and trading titles—these makeshift policies of a declining age are the fault of those who manage state finance.

sentences.zh: 臣請痛抑末技，嚴禁遊惰，斥異端使歸南畝，裁冗員以省虛糜。

translations.literal: Your servant asks to sternly suppress secondary crafts, strictly forbid idleness and wandering, drive heterodox pursuits back to the southern fields, and cut redundant posts to save empty waste.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant asks that secondary crafts be sternly suppressed, idleness strictly forbidden, heterodox pursuits driven back to the fields, and redundant posts cut to end wasteful spending.

sentences.zh: 開屯田而實邊，料士伍而紓餉。

translations.literal: Open garrison farms to strengthen the frontier, assess military households to ease transport of provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Open garrison farms to strengthen the frontier and assess military households to ease the burden of transport.

sentences.zh: 寺觀營造，供佛飯僧，以及不急之工，無益之費，悉行停罷。

translations.literal: Temple and monastery construction, supplying Buddha and feeding monks, as well as non-urgent works and useless expenses—all should be halted.
translations.idiomatic: Temple and monastery construction, supplying Buddha and feeding monks, and all non-urgent works and useless expenses should be halted.

sentences.zh: 專以務農重粟為本，而躬行節儉以先之，然後可阜民而裕國也。

translations.literal: Devote oneself to agriculture and grain as the foundation, and personally practice frugality to lead the way; only then may the people be enriched and the state made prosperous.
translations.idiomatic: Make agriculture and grain the foundation, and personally practice frugality to lead the way; only then may the people be enriched and the state made prosperous.

sentences.zh: 倘忍不加務，任掊克聚斂之臣行朝三暮四之術，民力已盡而征發無已，民財已竭而賦斂日增。

translations.literal: If one bears it and does not exert effort, entrusting extortionate and tax-gathering ministers to practice the trick of changing terms morning and evening, the people's strength already exhausted yet levies and conscription unending, the people's wealth already drained yet tax collection increasing daily.
translations.idiomatic: If nothing is done, and extortionate tax-gathering ministers are allowed to practice bait-and-switch policies, the people's strength will be exhausted while levies and conscription never cease, and the people's wealth drained while taxes rise daily.

sentences.zh: 茍紓目前之急，不恤意外之虞，臣竊懼焉。

translations.literal: If one merely relieves the present emergency and does not care for unforeseen dangers, your servant privately fears this.
translations.idiomatic: If the present emergency alone is relieved while unforeseen dangers are ignored, your servant privately fears the consequences.

sentences.zh: 章下戶部。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 尚書金濂請解職，帝不許。

translations.literal: Minister Jin Lian requested to resign his post; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Jin Lian requested to resign; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 鼎言亦不盡行。

translations.literal: Ding's proposals were also not fully implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Ding's proposals were also not fully implemented.

sentences.zh: 逾月，以災異，偕同官陳救弊恤民七事。

translations.literal: After a month, because of calamities and anomalies, together with his colleagues he set forth seven matters for remedying abuses and comforting the people.
translations.idiomatic: A month later, citing calamities and portents, he joined his colleagues in setting forth seven measures to remedy abuses and relieve the people.

sentences.zh: 末言：「大臣不乏奸回，宜黜罷其尤，用清政本。」

translations.literal: At the end he said: "Among high ministers there are no lack of treacherous villains; the worst should be dismissed and removed, to clarify the foundation of government."
translations.idiomatic: At the end he said: "Among high ministers there are no lack of treacherous villains; the worst should be dismissed and removed to clarify the foundation of government."

sentences.zh: 帝善其言，下詔甄別，而大臣辭職並慰留。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words, issued an edict to sort them out, but the ministers all submitted resignations and were comforted and retained.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his words and issued an edict to sort them out, but the ministers all submitted resignations and were comforted and retained.

sentences.zh: 給事中林聰請明諭鼎等指實劾奏，鼎、聰等乃共論吏部尚書何文淵、刑部尚書俞士悅、工部侍郎張敏、通政使李錫不職狀。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Lin Cong requested a clear instruction that Ding and the others impeach by naming specifics; Ding, Cong, and the others then jointly charged Minister of Personnel He Wenyuan, Minister of Justice Yu Shiyue, Vice Minister of Works Zhang Min, and Transmission Commissioner Li Xi with dereliction of duty.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Lin Cong asked that Ding and the others be clearly instructed to impeach by naming specifics; Ding, Cong, and the others then jointly charged Minister of Personnel He Wenyuan, Minister of Justice Yu Shiyue, Vice Minister of Works Zhang Min, and Transmission Commissioner Li Xi with dereliction of duty.

sentences.zh: 錫罷，文淵致仕。

translations.literal: Li was dismissed; He retired.
translations.idiomatic: Li was dismissed and He retired from office.

sentences.zh: 鼎居官清勤，卓有聲譽。

translations.literal: Ding in office was pure and diligent, with outstanding reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Ding served with integrity and diligence and enjoyed an outstanding reputation.

sentences.zh: 御史練綱以敢言名，而鼎尤善為章奏。

translations.literal: Censor Lian Gang was famed for bold speech, while Ding was especially skilled at composing memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Lian Gang was famed for bold speech, while Ding was especially skilled at composing memorials.

sentences.zh: 京師語曰：「左鼎手，練綱口。」

translations.literal: A saying in the capital ran: "Zuo Ding's hand, Lian Gang's mouth."
translations.idiomatic: A saying in the capital ran: "Zuo Ding's hand, Lian Gang's mouth."

sentences.zh: 自公卿以下咸憚之。

translations.literal: From dukes and ministers downward, all feared them.
translations.idiomatic: From dukes and ministers downward, all feared them.

sentences.zh: 鼎出為廣東右參政。

translations.literal: Ding went out as Right Administrative Commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Ding was appointed Right Administrative Commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 會英宗復位，以郭登言，召為左僉都御史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong regained the throne, on Guo Deng's recommendation he was summoned as Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong regained the throne, on Guo Deng's recommendation he was summoned back as Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 逾年卒。

translations.literal: After a year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year.

sentences.zh: 練綱，字從道，長洲人。

translations.literal: Lian Gang, courtesy name Congdao, was a man of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lian Gang, courtesy name Congdao, was a native of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖則成，洪武時御史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ze Cheng was a censor in the Hongwu reign.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ze Cheng had been a censor in the Hongwu reign.

sentences.zh: 綱舉鄉試，入國子監。

translations.literal: Gang passed the provincial examination and entered the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Gang passed the provincial examination and entered the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 歷事都察院。

translations.literal: He served in the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 郕王監國，上中興八策。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Cheng acted as regent, he submitted the Eight Policies for Restoration.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Cheng acted as regent, he submitted the Eight Policies for Restoration.

sentences.zh: 也先將入犯，復言：「和議不可就，南遷不可從，有持此議者，宜立誅。

translations.literal: When Esen was about to invade, he spoke again: "Peace talks must not be concluded, southern relocation must not be followed; whoever holds such views should be immediately executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen was about to invade, he spoke again: "Peace talks must not be concluded, southern relocation must not be followed; whoever holds such views should be immediately executed.

sentences.zh: 安危所倚，惟于謙、石亨當主中軍，而分遣大臣守九門，擇親王忠孝著聞者，令同守臣勤王。

translations.literal: On whom safety and peril depend, only Yu Qian and Shi Heng should command the central army; dispatch grand ministers to hold the Nine Gates; select princes renowned for loyalty and filial piety and have them join defenders in calling for relief troops.
translations.idiomatic: The fate of the realm depends on Yu Qian and Shi Heng commanding the central army; grand ministers should be dispatched to hold the Nine Gates, and princes renowned for loyalty and filial piety should be chosen to join the defenders in calling for relief troops.

sentences.zh: 檄陜西守將調番兵入衛。」

translations.literal: Order the Shaanxi frontier commanders to mobilize fan troops to enter and defend the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Order the Shaanxi frontier commanders to mobilize frontier troops to enter and defend the capital."

sentences.zh: 帝悉從之。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted all of it.

sentences.zh: 綱有才辨，急功名。

translations.literal: Gang had talent and eloquence, eager for fame and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Gang was talented and eloquent, and eager for fame and achievement.

sentences.zh: 都御史陳鎰、尚書俞士悅皆綱同里，念綱數陳是政有聲，且畏其口，遂薦之，授御史。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Chen Yi and Minister Yu Shiyue were all Gang's fellow townsmen; mindful that Gang had repeatedly set forth correct policies with reputation, and also fearing his mouth, they recommended him and he was appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Chen Yi and Minister Yu Shiyue were fellow townsmen of Gang's; mindful that Gang had repeatedly set forth sound policies with growing reputation, and also fearing his sharp tongue, they recommended him and he was appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 景泰改元，上時政五事。

translations.literal: When the Jingtai reign title was changed, he submitted five matters on current policy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingtai reign title was adopted, he submitted five matters on current policy.

sentences.zh: 巡視兩淮鹽政。

translations.literal: He inspected the salt administration of the Two Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected the salt administration of the Two Huai.

sentences.zh: 駙馬都尉趙輝侵利，劾奏之。

translations.literal: Chief Commandant of Escorts Zhao Hui encroached on profits; he impeached and memorialized against him.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Chief Commandant of Escorts Zhao Hui for encroaching on profits.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，偕同官應詔陳八事，並允行。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year, together with fellow officials he responded to an imperial edict and set forth eight matters; all were approved and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year, he and his fellow officials responded to an imperial edict with eight proposals, all of which were approved and carried out.

sentences.zh: 亡何，復偕同官上言：「吏部推選不公，任情高下，請置尚書何文淵、右侍郎項文曜於理。

translations.literal: Before long, again together with fellow officials he submitted a memorial: "The Ministry of Personnel's recommendations are unjust, raising and lowering ranks at whim; we ask that Minister He Wenyuan and Right Vice Minister Xiang Wenyao be brought to justice.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, he again joined his fellow officials in a memorial: "The Ministry of Personnel's recommendations are unjust, with ranks raised or lowered at whim. We ask that Minister He Wenyuan and Right Vice Minister Xiang Wenyao be held accountable.

sentences.zh: 尚書王直、左侍郎俞山素行本端，為文曜等所罔，均宜按問。」

translations.literal: Minister Wang Zhi and Left Vice Minister Yu Shan have always been upright in conduct but were misled by Xiang Wenyao and others; all should be investigated."
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wang Zhi and Left Vice Minister Yu Shan have always been upright in conduct, yet were misled by Xiang Wenyao and others; all of them should be investigated."

sentences.zh: 帝雖不罪，終以綱等為直。

translations.literal: Although the emperor did not punish them, he ultimately regarded Gang and the others as in the right.
translations.idiomatic: Although the emperor did not punish anyone, he ultimately regarded Gang and his colleagues as in the right.

sentences.zh: 明年命出贊延綏軍務，自陳名輕責重，乞授僉都御史。

translations.literal: The next year he was ordered out to assist in Yan-Sui military affairs; he stated that his reputation was slight while his responsibility was heavy, and begged to be granted the post of Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was ordered to assist in military affairs on the Yan-Sui frontier. He argued that his reputation was slight for so heavy a responsibility and asked to be granted the rank of Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「遷官可自求耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Can one seek one's own promotion?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Can one seek one's own promotion?"

sentences.zh: 遂寢其命。

translations.literal: Thereupon the appointment was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the appointment was shelved.

sentences.zh: 初，京師戒嚴，募四方民壯分營訓練，歲久多逃，或赴操不如期，廷議編之尺籍。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the capital was under martial law, able-bodied men from all quarters were recruited, divided into camps, and trained; after many years many fled, or failed to report for drill on time, and the court debated enrolling them in the military registers.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the capital was under martial law, able-bodied men from across the realm had been recruited, divided into camps, and trained. After many years many had fled or failed to report for drill on time, and the court debated enrolling them in the military registers.

sentences.zh: 綱等言：「召募之初，激以忠義，許事定罷遣。

translations.literal: Gang and others said: "At the outset of recruitment they were stirred by loyalty and righteousness, and it was promised that when affairs were settled they would be dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Gang and his colleagues argued: "At the outset of recruitment they were stirred by appeals to loyalty and righteousness, with a promise that once affairs were settled they would be dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 今展轉輪操，已孤所望，況其逃亡，實迫寒餒，豈可遽著軍籍。

translations.literal: Now they are rotated through drill again and again, already betraying what was hoped; moreover their flight is truly driven by cold and hunger—how can they suddenly be entered in the military rolls?
translations.idiomatic: Now they are rotated through drill again and again, already a betrayal of what was promised; moreover their flight is truly driven by cold and hunger. How can they suddenly be entered in the military rolls?

sentences.zh: 邊方多故，倘更召募，誰復應之？」

translations.literal: The frontier has many troubles; if recruitment is attempted again, who will respond?"
translations.idiomatic: The frontier has many troubles; if recruitment is attempted again, who will answer the call?"

sentences.zh: 詔即除前令。

translations.literal: An edict immediately revoked the earlier order.
translations.idiomatic: An edict immediately revoked the earlier order.

sentences.zh: 五年巡按福建，與按察使楊玨互訐，俱下吏。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, while touring and inspecting Fujian, he and Surveillance Commissioner Yang Jue mutually impeached each other; both were handed over to the officials for trial.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, while serving as touring inspector of Fujian, he and Surveillance Commissioner Yang Jue mutually impeached each other, and both were handed over to the authorities for trial.

sentences.zh: 謫玨黃州知府，綱邠州判官。

translations.literal: Jue was demoted to prefect of Huangzhou; Gang to magistrate of Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jue was demoted to prefect of Huangzhou, and Gang to magistrate of Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 久之卒。

translations.literal: After a long while he died.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he died.

sentences.zh: 曹凱，字宗元，益都人。

translations.literal: Cao Kai, courtesy name Zongyuan, was a native of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Kai, courtesy name Zongyuan, was a native of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 正統十年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the tenth year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the tenth year of the Zhengtong reign.

sentences.zh: 授刑科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Bureau of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Bureau of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 磊落多壯節。

translations.literal: Open and forthright, with many bold acts.
translations.idiomatic: He was open and forthright, with many bold acts to his name.

sentences.zh: 英宗北征，諫甚力，且曰：「今日之勢，大異澶淵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong marched north, he remonstrated with great force and said: "Today's situation differs greatly from Chanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong marched north, he remonstrated forcefully and said, "Today's situation differs greatly from Chanyuan.

sentences.zh: 彼文武忠勇，士馬勁悍。

translations.literal: There the civil and military officials were loyal and brave, and troops and horses strong and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: There the civil and military officials were loyal and brave, and the troops and horses strong and fierce.

sentences.zh: 今中貴竊權，人心玩愒。

translations.literal: Now eunuchs usurp power, and men's hearts are lax and indifferent.
translations.idiomatic: Now eunuchs usurp power, and men's hearts are lax and indifferent.

sentences.zh: 此輩不惟以陛下為孤註，即懷、湣、徽、欽亦何暇恤？」

translations.literal: These men not only treat Your Majesty as a lone wager, but even Huai, Min, Hui, and Qin—what leisure have they to care for them?"
translations.idiomatic: These men not only treat Your Majesty as a lone wager, but even the spirits of Huai, Min, Hui, and Qin—what leisure have they to care for them?"

sentences.zh: 帝不從，乘輿果陷。

translations.literal: The emperor did not heed him, and the imperial carriage indeed fell into disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed him, and the imperial carriage indeed fell into disaster.

sentences.zh: 凱痛哭竟日，聲徹禁庭，與王竑共擊馬順至死。

translations.literal: Kai wept bitterly all day, his voice reaching through the forbidden court; together with Wang Hong he beat Ma Shun to death.
translations.idiomatic: Kai wept bitterly all day, his voice reaching through the forbidden court, and together with Wang Hong he beat Ma Shun to death.

sentences.zh: 景泰中，遷左。

translations.literal: During the Jingtai reign he was transferred to the left.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingtai reign he was transferred to the left post.

sentences.zh: 給事中林聰劾何文淵、周旋，詔宥之。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Lin Cong impeached He Wenyuan and Zhou Xuan; an edict pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Lin Cong impeached He Wenyuan and Zhou Xuan, but an edict pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 凱上殿力諍，二人遂下吏。

translations.literal: Kai entered the hall and remonstrated forcefully; the two men were then handed over to the officials.
translations.idiomatic: Kai entered the hall and remonstrated forcefully, and the two men were then handed over to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 時令輸豆得補官，凱爭曰：「近例，輸豆四千石以上，授指揮。

translations.literal: At the time it was ordered that submitting beans could qualify one for an official post; Kai contended: "By recent precedent, submitting four thousand piculs of beans or more grants the rank of commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the time it was ordered that submitting beans could qualify one for an official post. Kai objected: "By recent precedent, submitting four thousand piculs of beans or more grants the rank of commander.

sentences.zh: 彼受祿十餘年，費已償矣，乃令之世襲，是以生民膏血養無功子孫，而彼取息長無窮也。

translations.literal: They have received salaries for more than ten years—the cost is already repaid—yet they are allowed to pass the post down in hereditary succession; thus the fat and blood of the people nourish undeserving descendants, while they draw interest forever without end.
translations.idiomatic: They have drawn salaries for more than ten years—the cost is already repaid—yet they are allowed to pass the post down in hereditary succession. Thus the sweat and blood of the people nourish undeserving descendants, while they draw profit without end.

sentences.zh: 有功者必相謂曰：吾以捐軀獲此，彼以輸豆亦獲此，是朝廷以我軀命等於荏菽，其誰不解體！
